articles.title_orig: Newly Elected US Senators Define Their Positions on China - VOA
articles.title_zh: Newly Elected US Senators Define Their Positions on China - VOA
articles.content_orig:
Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Mandarin article .
From advanced semiconductor exports to Taiwan’s defense and agricultural trade, newly elected U.S. senators have outlined a range of priorities for relations with China. Their campaign platforms and legislative records offer a look at the issues they could pursue when the next Congress convenes in January.
Among the incoming Democrats, some favor tighter technology controls and stronger support for Taiwan while questioning the economic costs of tariffs. Newly elected Republicans have advocated measures addressing arms sales, supply chains and competition affecting industries in their home states.
However, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said President Donald Trump would determine U.S. policy as he sees fit, regardless of how Republicans fared in the midterm elections.
“Congress has a role to play in our foreign policy, particularly on what it funds and in its oversight function, but the No. 1 factor in determining foreign policy has always been and will remain the president,” Rubio said.
In a Nov. 5 newsletter, the New York based ChinaTalk examined the campaign platforms and records of 12 newly elected senators, highlighting their differing priorities on trade, technology and Taiwan. ChinaTalk describes itself as a hybrid think tank and media outlet focused on China and emerging technology. Trade and technology Texas Democrat James Talarico advocates legislation enforcing and strengthening export controls to keep advanced super intelligence (commonly referred to artificial intelligence) chips from adversaries who could use them against the United States. He also wants data centers to pay for infrastructure they require rather than pass costs to households.
Illinois Democrat Juliana Stratton criticized Trump’s China trade tariffs in a Chicago Sun-Times candidate questionnaire, saying tariffs increase household and agricultural costs. She favors investment in infrastructure, technology and workers, while protecting intellectual property and data from Chinese cybersecurity threats and supporting Taiwan’s self-defense.
Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed argues that competition with China need not lead to military conflict. His platform supports competition through research and economic strength alongside cooperation on shared interests. His SI proposals nevertheless include computing controls, customer identification requirements for computing providers and an independent safety-testing agency.
Taiwan’s bipartisan support
New Hampshire Democrat Chris Pappas has pursued legislation addressing Taiwan’s defense, international participation and diplomatic representation.
In 2023, he joined Republican Jim Banks in introducing the Taiwan Peace Through Strength Act, seeking faster arms sales, expanded military training and exchanges, and access to critical munitions.
Pappas also backed proposals in 2022 and 2025 to rename Taiwan’s representative office in Washington the “Taiwan Representative Office.” According to ChinaTalk, he supported Taiwan’s participation as a World Health Assembly observer and in World Health Organization technical meetings.
Kentucky Republican Andy Barr joined Democrat Ami Bera in questioning Secretary of State Marco Rubio in June about proposed Taiwan arms sales, reported delays and the administration’s commitment to longstanding Taiwan policy.
Local industries and economic security
Louisiana Republican Julia Letlow helped introduce the Safer Shrimp Imports Act in 2025, seeking stronger food-safety oversight. She also joined calls for a Section 301 investigation into unfair seafood trade practices. ChinaTalk identified competition from Chinese seafood imports among her concerns.
Oklahoma Republican Kevin Hern introduced the Countering Communist China Act in 2024, addressing investment, supply chains, research, education, Taiwan and defense. His proposals include disclosure of Chinese Communist Party funding for think tanks and nonprofits, restrictions on paid lobbying, and sanctions targeting senior party officials involved in threats to Taiwan’s sovereignty.
These positions are proposals and records, not decisions by the next Congress. Senators can introduce legislation, conduct oversight and consider presidential nominations, but individual preferences do not establish party consensus.
Their congressional influence will depend on committee assignments, negotiations and legislative support. The U.S. president ultimately retains a leading role in diplomacy and policy implementation, along with the power to veto legislation.
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said a Democratic-controlled Congress in January would not change the administration’s approach to foreign policy, emphasizing that the president has primary authority over its direction.
Rubio said Congress has a role in funding, appropriations and oversight, but added that “it won’t influence or change the President’s directives in terms of what he was elected to do. The president was elected to execute the foreign policy of the United States. That is a function of the executive branch.”

articles.title_orig: Russia and Ukraine hold nearly 4 hours of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.title_zh: Russia and Ukraine hold nearly 4 hours of US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.content_orig:
Senior officials from Ukraine, Russia and the US will reconvene for a second day of talks on Wednesday
The first of two days of trilateral talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US aimed at ending the war in Ukraine has concluded in Abu Dhabi.
While senior officials from Kyiv and Moscow were tight-lipped after the four hour-long discussions, President Volodymyr Zelensky, who was not at the talks, said they had proved "constructive and quite substantive".
Speaking from Paris, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio also said the meeting had been "very productive".
Although expectations for a breakthrough that ends Russia's full-scale war on Ukraine are low, US officials said earlier that Moscow and Kyiv were privately showing "a little bit of flexibility" on the issue of who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar scenario.
Zelensky also said that humanitarian issues such as prisoner of war exchanges had been discussed.
At the start of Tuesday's talks President Donald Trump's son-in-law, Jared Kushner, told delegates that the US had "narrowed the gaps" between the two sides, without providing details, and hoped to move towards a "solution that hopefully ends the war".
Kushner had said earlier the talks would be focused on addressing the "postwar security concerns" of both Russia and Ukraine.
He and Trump peace envoy Steve Witkoff also met Ukrainian and European and Nato officials on the sidelines of the main meeting.
Until now European leaders have largely been excluded from peace talks, but they have pushed to be included in the discussions amid concerns that decisions about their continent's security would be made without them.
The Americans appear to support this, with Rubio acknowledging during a visit to Paris that the Europeans "are a part of solving this problem for the long term".
However, "the Russians have a bad taste in their mouth with the Europeans", according to a US official.
Some proposals favoured by EU officials - such as calling an unconditional ceasefire as a prerequisite for peace negotiations - are routinely rejected by Moscow. Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said on Tuesday that a truce would just allow Kyiv to regroup. "We will not agree to it," he said.
Moscow and Kyiv's positions are still far apart on ending the conflict.
A key area of disagreement involves Ukraine's eastern region of Donetsk, which is mostly occupied by Russia.
Moscow has demanded that Ukraine relinquish the parts of Donetsk it still holds, while Kyiv wants to freeze the contact line to maintain control over those areas, which it says are crucial to its future security.
While neither side has budged on these demands, the US official speaking on the eve of the talks suggested that this was just the public stance and that Moscow and Kyiv had shown "a little bit of flexibility, privately".
However, he acknowledged the issue would not be solved without discussions about a new "security architecture".
"They will not solve the Donetsk issue and the territorial issue until they know what the security architecture is going to be after the war," the official said. "And keep in mind, we're not going to be able to finalise one without the other."
For Ukraine, a post-war "security architecture" may include reassurance that allies will come to its aid if it comes under attack again. For Russia, that could be its longstanding ambition to see Nato roll back from Eastern Europe â which would be alarming to Europeans.
The framework being proposed includes security consultations and crisis communications hotlines, as well as "reciprocal de-escalation measures" between the two. The officials also floated the re-activation of the Nato-Russia Council that has been largely paused since 2022.
Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff are part of the US delegation that will attend the talks in Abu Dhabi
The last round of trilateral talks, held in Geneva in February, ended without a breakthrough. Soon after, the US-Israel war on Iran diverted Washington's attention from Ukraine, and no other discussions were held since.
From the start of his second term in office, US President Donald Trump â who once boasted he could end the war in Ukraine within a day â has spearheaded several rounds of talks to end the conflict, albeit with little success.
Meanwhile, his increasingly conciliatory approach towards Moscow has fuelled deep unease in Kyiv and across the European Union.
After meeting Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev in Washington last week, Trump touted a forthcoming "big, beautiful agreement" on Ukraine that "might involve all of Europe".
Many in Ukraine are sceptical that this would result in a fair peace.
Ukrainian MP Oleksandr Merezhko, head of the foreign affairs parliamentary committee, told the BBC he believed Trump wanted "a quick deal at the expense of Ukraine", which will certainly be rejected by Kyiv.
The only way to make Russia's Vladimir Putin start real negotiations was by putting greater pressure on Russia through sanctions and deep strikes, Merezhko said.
"While Putin has a war machine up and running, he has no incentives to negotiate." He also mentioned recent moves by Trump, such as his deal to buy diesel from Russia, as something that "only encourages Moscow to continue the war".
Moscow's delegation in Abu Dhabi includes Kremlin aide Vladimir Medinsky, deputy foreign ministers Sergei Ryabkov and Mikhail Galuzin, spy chief Igor Kostyukov and army general Yury Zhigarlovsky.
Kyiv has sent several senior officials who have been part of previous negotiating teams, including Foreign Intelligence Service head Rustem Umerov, Volodymyr Zelensky's chief of staff Kyrylo Budanov, and MP Davyd Arakhamiya.
Away from Abu Dhabi, Russia continues to pummel Ukraine with deadly bombardments and strikes on energy infrastructure, viewed in Kyiv as proof that Moscow wants to corner Ukraine into accepting a deal on Russia's terms.
On Monday, Kushner was cautious to point out that the Abu Dhabi talks could at most "build momentum toward the next phase of negotiations".
"This is an extraordinarily difficult and complicated conflict," he wrote on X, adding the US was "approaching these discussions with determination and realism."

articles.title_orig: Dublin: Arrests made after visit from former US President Biden
articles.title_zh: Dublin: Arrests made after visit from former US President Biden
articles.content_orig:
Hundreds of women have come forward with abuse allegations against the former Harrods and Ritz Paris owner
French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse.
The Paris prosecutor's office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released.
In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities.
It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner.
Mohamed Al Fayed accused of multiple rapes by staff
Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor's office said.
It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into "allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape".
The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed.
The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family.
The Villa Windsor in western Paris, another property involved in the search, was a holiday home for the Al Fayed family. It was previously the home of King Edward VIII, following his abdication, and his wife Wallis Simpson.
The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims:
"At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities.
"In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-ThÃ©rÃ¨se in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators.
"Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations.
"The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office."
A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation.
The Ritz hotel in Paris is still owned by the Al Fayed family
Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024.
One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence.
Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers.
A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed's brother , Salah Fayed, who died in 2010.
Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations.
Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate.
In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims.
"Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further."
The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities.
"We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said.
"We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated."
The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like.
"Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over."
The management of the Ritz Paris told AFP news agency that it "does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour" and that it was ready "to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities".
If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support is available at BBC Action Line .

articles.title_orig: Nvidia CEO’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy could be a problem for the economy
articles.title_zh: Nvidia CEO’s affair with an alleged Chinese spy could be a problem for the economy
articles.content_orig:
Rep. John Moolenaar , R-Mich., said on a Tuesday appearance on CNBC's "Squawk Box" that Congress needs to "get to the bottom" of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang 's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
Moolenaar, who chairs the House Permanent Select Committee on China, said he wants to know whether Huang shared privileged information with a Chinese spy; whether Huang was influenced to lobby against preventing chip sales to China; and whether China was given preference in purchasing Nvidia's limited supply of advanced chips.
And he urged a thorough internal investigation of Huang.
"If it becomes less of an investigation, more of damage control, that's not going to work because people have to have confidence," Moolenaar said.
"We're dealing with the country, the Chinese Communist Party that is a foremost adversary, that's funding wars and supporting Russia, supporting Iran, North Korea," he said. "And we have basically a Cold War race with technology. We cannot allow the premier company at the forefront of this to, in some way, be irresponsible."
Congressional scrutiny of Huang's affair has intensified since members returned to Washington on Monday.
The New York Times reported that Huang was romantically involved with Alice Huang, a Megaspeed executive who U.S. intelligence agencies have identified as a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia opened an investigation into its CEO on Sunday. The two Huangs are not related.
Rep. Jay Obernolte, R-Calif., co-chair of the House AI task force, raised concerns that the scandal could plague talks over export controls for advanced AI chips. "It's important not to have a personal scandal interfere with the substantive policy discussion about to what degree we should be allowing the export of cutting edge chips to our geopolitical competitors like China," Obernolte told CNBC. "I hope this isn't a distraction because that's a very important conversation that needs to happen."
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries , D-N.Y., said in a press conference on Monday that "we're going to need a full briefing specifically as it relates to the Nvidia issue so we can all get to the bottom of what has happened and what the implications are in terms of national security"
Moolenaar co-authored a letter with Florida Rep. Brian Mast and Arkansas Rep. Rick Crawford on Nov. 5 asking Huang to appear before the Select Committee on China, the House Foreign Affairs Committee and House Select Committee on Intelligence. Mast chairs the foreign affairs panel, and Crawford chairs intelligence.
"Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information," the three Republicans wrote.
Mast said Tuesday he did not know whether Huang had responded to the letter he authored with Moolenar and Crawford demanding the tech CEO brief them. "I can't say that I've heard an answer back yet that," Mast told reporters at the Capitol. Mast then rattled off a list of questions he has for Huang, including where the company has been selling chips, what Megaspeed may have been using them for, who has been remotely accessing Nvidia chips and what information was passed between Huang and the potential spy. "Obviously questions relating to his relationship and what information was or was not passed about anything," Mast said when asked what he wants answered.
Mast said he "can't say it would hurt" to hear from the Commerce Department as well, noting he speaks regularly to the Bureau of Industry and Security. "So that's obviously something that falls directly under Commerce," he said

articles.title_orig: US and rest of world must follow China’s lead on green energy, says John Kerry
articles.title_zh: US and rest of world must follow China’s lead on green energy, says John Kerry
articles.content_orig:
Former US secretary of state says most nations are ‘stumbling along’ while Beijing has ‘hugely accelerated’
Cop31 live – latest updates
China is leading the world in moving away from fossil fuels , and the rest of the globe – including the US – must now follow, the former US secretary of state John Kerry has told the Guardian, as Cop watchers wonder exactly how China is going to approach this year’s climate summit.
As Cop31 opens – this year the climate conference is in Turkey – there is plenty of speculation about whether China will finally step into the leadership role that it has long avoided. In its latest “five-year plan” adopted in March 2026, China for the first time pledged to “actively participate in and lead global climate governance”. Cop31 could provide the first indications Beijing is ready to put that rhetoric into action, something it has historically been reluctant to do.
Green energy is a vital component of the export engine that has kept China’s sluggish post-pandemic economy on track. The success of its exports stands in contrast to its failure to significantly boost domestic general consumption, a structural weakness that has persistently vexed leaders.
In 2025, clean-tech exports surpassed $220bn, and they should grow again this year; the world’s largest emitter is now the world’s leading supplier of clean energy technology. China accounts for about 85% of solar and 80% of lithium-ion battery supply chain production capacity, and in 2025, nearly 75% of electric cars were manufactured there.
Smart moves now by China would position it as a linchpin in a future electrostate world order, persuade rivals to cooperate, and solidify its influence in the global south.
Meanwhile other countries, including the US under Donald Trump, have fallen badly behind. Kerry said they would lose out economically – as well as putting the climate in further danger – unless they, too, embraced low-carbon power and rapid electrification. “The only country that has hugely accelerated is China. The rest of the world is stumbling along while Mother Nature is sending us more powerful signals every week, every day,” he said.
“[China] realised suddenly they had way too much dependency on oil and gas from other places, and they decided they needed to be independent. Other countries, since the war in Iran, and since the strait of Hormuz has been interrupted, have made a similar decision, and they’re moving independently. There’s been a massive uptick in deployment of renewables. Thank you, Donald Trump.”
For autocratic states without free and fair elections , seeing the economic benefits reaped by China would be the spur to adopt low-carbon growth, he added.
“They’ll see where the market is going, and they will recognise where the cheaper alternatives are. Even they can read a spreadsheet, and understand where costs are exorbitant [in fossil fuels], and where you have a better deal,” Kerry said. “Right now, renewables together with storage, together with some transitional gas, is cheaper and more effective, than just going with fossil fuels.”
He added: “The marketplace has made its decision and globally is moving to electrons, and electrostate status. People are going to electricity and they’re going to try to do that as clean as humanly possible. That’s the choice that I see being implemented in many different places. It is unstoppable.”
China has already said it wants Cop31 to discuss the free flow of green technology against a backdrop of “intensifying” geopolitical conflicts – widely seen as a reference to US and EU tariffs on items such as Chinese electric vehicles and solar products.
Li Shuo from the Asia Society Policy Institute (ASPI) puts it this way : “In a world where climate action was once seen as a constraint on growth but is now increasingly a driver of it, China faces a singular question: will it step into a leadership role not out of obligation, but out of self-interest?”
The summit’s presidency has promised this Cop will be one of “implementation and acceleration” – and when it comes to the green transition, nowhere has implemented or accelerated quite like China. As a result, emissions have been in a “flat or falling” trend since March 2024, analysis for Carbon Brief shows .
Beijing sees the energy transition as “central to economic modernisation and energy security, with significant implications for international influence”, said Kevin Tu from the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies. The wars in Ukraine and the Middle East and their effect on oil and gas supplies have only hardened that stance.
The conflicts have also highlighted the geopolitical implications of a planetary shift to green energy. In the fossil fuel era, the designation of the US dollar as the global trading currency for oil gave Washington “what has been termed the exorbitant privilege of being the global lender of last resort”, said Isabel Hilton, the founder of the specialist environment outlet China Dialogue.
after newsletter promotion
“Without that, the US position in the world looks weaker, and if you add China’s dominance of the supply of clean technologies and the supply chains that produce them, US dominance looks more vulnerable still.”
Meanwhile, President Xi Jinping describes China as a “doer and go-getter working for the cause of global development” and state media frequently showcase Chinese renewable projects in countries ranging from Indonesia to Pakistan and Kenya. The value of the green energy deals in China’s belt and road initiative in the first half of 2026 has already surpassed the total for the whole of 2025, a recent analysis showed .
Those countries could be useful allies if China can get the subject of tariffs into the talks. “China is likely to find support from Brazil, India, South Africa and other developing countries concerned about the costs and market-access effects of climate-related trade measures,” said Tu.
China has generally held back from policy ambition or agenda-setting at forums such as Cop. Its attitude to the plans to set a global target for electrification has been ambivalent, even though it would easily hit it, according to ASPI’s Kate Logan. Partly, China has an aversion to prescriptive outside targets, but it is also trying to navigate the divergent interests of its global south partners.
Yixian Sun, a professor of sustainability governance at the University of Bath, said: “I still think there is a mismatch between Chinese policymakers’ views on the role that China can play in global climate governance and international expectations on the influence that China should exert.”
If the world wants China to play a leadership role, the environment needs to change, and more trust extended, he says. “They have to be ready to accept China’s leadership, and I don’t think this is the case, especially for global north countries”.
Analysts will watch China’s actions around climate finance commitments and support for a “just transition” – a framework designed to secure workers’ rights and livelihoods in the move away from fossil fuels.
They will also be looking for signals Beijing will bid for Cop33 in 2028; officials are said to be trying to decide if hosting would be beneficial.
For now, said Logan, “China would be happy with a Cop that doesn’t necessarily produce anything monumental, but comes out with a relatively cooperative outcome … so no major drama.”

articles.title_orig: Google Fi brings back network switching with ‘secondary’ partner, expands W+ beyond Pixel
articles.title_zh: Google Fi brings back network switching with ‘secondary’ partner, expands W+ beyond Pixel
articles.content_orig:
Google Fi Wireless is rolling out a big update today with the return of network switching thanks to a “secondary” partner.
At the beginning, Project Fi was known for giving subscribers access to both T-Mobile and Sprint networks. Over time, the second partner went away, leaving one predominant network.
Google Fi is now bringing back a second partner as part of its new “super network.” Most users will be on the “Primary network,” but Google Fi will automatically switch users to the “Secondary network” if it meaningfully improves performance with so-called “smart thresholds” for doing so. At launch, there is no manual switching.
Google is not naming the second network today, but did share that Ultra Wideband is supported. Officially, you are switching between “two of America’s fastest 5G networks.”
Fi Wireless does note that users have top priority, so data is never deprioritized on the Primary network. Meanwhile, there’s “highest QCI priority” on the backup network that means subscribers are among the last to be slowed down when there’s congestion. This is also available internationally when local partner networks are available with the Flexible and Unlimited Premium plans.
Network switching will first be supported on Pixel 9 and newer devices that have a Google Fi eSIM (and no other SIM active). It makes use of Android’s Multiple Enabled Profiles (MEP) eSIM technology that allows for two carrier profiles on a single chip.
The Google Fi app gains a “Your super network” card in the Home tab that shows whether you’re connected to the Primary or Secondary network. “See activity” lets you view switching history and when it last occurred. Google will also note if you’re in range of W+ networks.
Google today is also expanding its Wi-Fi Auto Connect+ network beyond Pixel phones to select Samsung Galaxy (S23, Fold/Flip 5, and newer) and modern Motorola phones. These premium Wi-Fi networks are available in millions of airports, malls, stores, and restaurants. The connection happens automatically, with the Google Fi Virtual Carrier Network encrypting data.
The final update today sees the companion app gain “Ask Fi.” This AI-powered chat is meant to quickly provide answers and guided troubleshooting for common issues. You can request human support with seamless handoff that keeps the chat context.

Micron's ( MU ) valuation has reached a level where it's simply too cheap to ignore given its fundamentals, says Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider.
Schneider reiterated his $1,250 price target on the once red-hot AI momentum trade. It assumes about 70% upside from current levels.
"We also believe risk/reward is becoming more attractive for Neutral-rated Micron in light of the high probability of strong free cash flow in the coming quarters," Schneider said.
Micron is currently approaching tangible book value, Schneider noted. When a stock trades below tangible book value, investors value the company at less than the estimated value of its assets after subtracting its liabilities and intangible assets.
In a sense, the market is saying the company's physical and financial assets are worth more than the entire company's stock market value.
That seems to be bordering on an unwarranted disconnect , at least in assessing Schneider's work on the chip player.
Micron's stock is down 17% over the past month amid fears that a blue wave on Election Day could slow the build-out of AI infrastructure. That could have ramifications for orders for Micron's memory chips.
The rout has brought Micron's forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio down to an almost laughable 4.2 times, according to Yahoo Finance AlphaSpace data. Keep in mind Micron is coming off a quarter of strong demand amid memory chip shortages driving up prices.
The Street still expects Micron to grow earnings by at least 17% in its next fiscal year.

articles.title_orig: China improving air connectivity with Central Asia, aiding trade and tourism
articles.title_zh: China improving air connectivity with Central Asia, aiding trade and tourism
articles.content_orig:
China and Central Asia are acting fast to expand air links. Chinese and Central Asian aviation officials gathered in Tashkent on November 3-5 for a Working Group session under the C5+1 format to improve implementation of existing agreements and review expansion plans. During the meeting, Kazakhstan agreed to raise permitted weekly flights from 150 to 180 and add routes to Chengdu and Kashgar . Uzbekistan, meanwhile, agreed to increase the number of weekly flights to China from 100 to 114.
Uzbekistan also proposed establishing new routes connecting Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan , and expanding weekly service between the two countries’ major cities, Tashkent, Almaty and Astana. Ahead of the conference, Air Astana and China Southern Airlines signed a strategic partnership agreement .  At the signing ceremony, Kazakhstan’s vice minister of transport said that flights between Kazakhstan and China had increased 52 percent year-on-year.
Underscoring an ambition to become Central Asia’s aviation hub for Europe-China traffic, Astana announced that it is working on a 25-year civil aviation master plan with the International Civil Aviation Organization. Work is progressing across Kazakhstan on modernizing airports in Almaty and Urzhar, in northern Kazakhstan near the Chinese border, constructing a second runway in Shymkent and completing new regional airports in Zaisan, Katonkaragay, and Kendirli.
Tajikistan and Turkmenistan are trying to keep pace with rising air traffic. Tajik President Emomali Rahmon ratified a five-year National Civil Aviation Safety Program running until 2031 that covers international air traffic growth , infrastructure modernization, and security preparedness; Turkmen President Serdar Berdymukhamedov endorsed measures to strengthen aviation safety .
On the sidelines of the Second Tien Shan Forum on Economic Cooperation in Central Asia, Kazakhstan and China discussed establishing a Kazakh-Chinese direct investment fund with initial capitalization of up to $200 million. Kazakh officials proposed consolidating existing and emerging financial mechanisms into a single Kazakh-Chinese project-financing and insurance window. Under the plan, several pilot projects would be selected to test the mechanism. If realized, the fund and single-window financing system would give Kazakhstan a more streamlined method of accessing Chinese capital and expand the use of the yuan in bilateral project finance.
At the China International Import Expo, Kazakh manufacturers signed agreements worth approximately $100 million . Details of the agreements and manufacturers involved were not disclosed.
Kazatomprom CEO Meirzhan Yussupov told President Kassym-Jomar Tokayev that the company secured new natural uranium supply agreements with major utilities in India and China. These deals reinforce China’s position as the main buyer of Kazakh uranium while signaling diversification toward India.
Negotiations are ongoing on building Kazakhstan’s second nuclear power plant nearly 18 months after Astana announced the selection of China’s National Nuclear Corporation as the preferred contractor. Kazakh Energy Ministry representatives have not specified what the holdup is. The delay leaves open the possibility that Astana could opt for the construction of small modular reactors (SMRs) that have been pitched by the United States or at least bring SMRs into Kazakhstan’s power-generating mix.
Kazakhstan is preparing to join a test of digital documentation for freight shipments between China and the Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU). The first digitally documented shipments covering coal, fertilizers, and consumer goods have begun moving through the Grodekovo-Suifenhe border crossing in Northeast China and Russia’s Far East. The Eurasian Economic Commission’s trade representative said documents authorizing similar shipments involving Kazakhstan could soon be ready for signature. Separately, Kazakhstan is developing a centralized, data-driven fiscal system that uses big data, cross-checking across systems, and AI to strengthen tax collection, price control and spending oversight. These efforts align Kazakhstan with China’s push for digital Belt and Road trade. Such a system would also help cement Astana’s role as China’s primary gateway to the EAEU.
In his address to the nation, President Tokayev said construction of the Bakhty-Ayagoz railway line is expected to launch in 2027. The line is expected to carry 20 million tons of freight annually, expanding Kazakhstan’s access to the Chinese market, while attracting additional transit traffic.
Kyrgyzstan China’s Ganfeng Lithium Group and the Kyrgyz National Investment Agency signed a memorandum of understanding covering mining-sector cooperation in Kyrgyzstan. The announcement offered no details on specific deposits, investment amounts or implementation timetable. Ganfeng is the world’s largest producer of lithium, which is classified as a critical material by the United States and other major global economies. Kyrgyzstan’s Eldik Bank and the Xinjiang branch of the Export-Import Bank of China signed a cooperation agreement during the Tian Shan Forum in Almaty. The agreement aims to attract long-term financing for infrastructure, transport and technology projects, including potential credit lines, leasing arrangements, trade finance and cross-border settlements. No specific loans, financing amounts or projects were announced. Kyrgyzstan’s Chamber of Commerce and Industry and the China-CentralAsia TechnologyTransfer Center signed an MoU to promote technology transfers, joint projects, specialist training and the development of technology parks in Kyrgyzstan. Details of the memo were not immediately disclosed. Tajikistan Tajikistan’s Ministry of Transport announced that it signed a construction agreement with Chinese contractor Nanjing Communication Engineering Company Ltd for reconstruction of the 54.1-kilometer Baljuvon-Sari Khosor road in Khatlon Province. The project includes 10 bridges and 121 drainage culverts and is financed through the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, which lists a sovereign loan of up to €49.2 million. On November 5, the Asia-Plus news agency reported that preliminary construction work was underway at 15 locations , involving 115 workers, including 40 Chinese nationals. The EBRD financing represents funding for the overall project, not the disclosed value of the Chinese contractor’s agreement, which was not specified.
Tajikistan and China also approved the findings of the feasibility study for a 90-kilometer stretch of the Murghab-Kulma highway. Construction is expected to begin in 2027, and will be funded by a Chinese grant, Caravan Info reports citing Tajikistan’s Ministry of Transport. Turkmenistan Turkmenistan’s Ministry of Industry and Construction Production and Chinese company Sany International Development Ltd. signed a memorandum of cooperation during an industry and energy conference in Ashgabat. A Ministry of Energy representative signed a separate memorandum with China’s TBEA Shenyang Transformer Group on energy-sector cooperation. The announcement did not specify investment amounts, implementation timetable or other details.
At a November 6-7 business forum in Shanghai, a Turkmen government-linked company, Ojar Aziya, sought funding from China for several projects, including a highway connecting Sarakhs, Mary and Serkhetabat and a logistics complex in Afghanistan’s Turgundi . The highway project has been on the drawing board since 2024. Beijing has given no sign that it is willing to finance either project.
Uzbekistan’s Minister of Construction met with the leadership of China State Construction International Corporation (CSCEC), a state-owned construction and engineering group. CSCEC has implemented several major projects in Uzbekistan, and the meeting focused on developing “ blueprints for roads and pipelines in the next batch of projects .” No specific initiatives were immediately announc

articles.title_orig: IBM to end visa, green card sponsorship for most roles in its Consulting arm
articles.title_zh: IBM to end visa, green card sponsorship for most roles in its Consulting arm
articles.content_orig:
Tech giant IBM is ending certain green card sponsorships for immigrant workers in part of its business, the company announced Tuesday.
The decision to halt H-1B and so-called PERM (Program Electronic Review Management) process applications for high-skilled workers within its consulting business comes amid the Trump administration 's crackdown on legal immigration that has seen other major tech companies, including Microsoft and Adobe , suspended from the green card program over fraud concerns.
Also known as “Labor Certification,” PERM is the first step of the most common green card category used by employers to sponsor an employee for permanent residence in the U.S.
"IBM Consulting participates in U.S. high-skilled visa programs to address skill shortages," an IBM spokesperson told Newsweek . "That participation has been declining for a number of years and as skill availability and client need have evolved, we have opted to discontinue visa and green card sponsorship for the majority of such roles in IBM Consulting."
Affected workers were told they could continue working for IBM outside the U.S. or leave the company at the end of the year, according to Bloomberg.
Newsweek has asked IBM for clarification on what would happen to workers on existing H-1Bs who would not be able to apply for a green card now.
U.S. Department of Labor data showed IBM applied for over 1,100 H-1B visas in Fiscal Year 2026—which ended on September 30—but it was not immediately clear how many visa holders then moved to become permanent residents.
Newsweek reached out to the Department of Labor and Department of Homeland Security for comment Tuesday morning.
The H-1B is one of the most well-known work visas in the U.S. Tech companies have, for many years, relied on the program to hire high-skilled foreign workers, but it has come under increasing scrutiny over concerns American-born workers are being pushed out of jobs in favor of cheaper labor.
Tens of thousands of applications are processed each year, with a large chunk being renewals. An H-1B initially lasts for three years, with the option to extend for a further three.
After that period ends, an employer must decide whether they want to keep a visa holder and apply for a green card for them. As part of that, they must prove no American-born workers are able to carry out the role by having advertised the position in certain places. Once that process is completed, they can apply for the green card.
While IBM is a consistent H-1B sponsor, it applies for relatively few visas each year compared to other major companies. Amazon applied for more than 13,715 visas by the third quarter of Fiscal Year 2026, 11 times that of IBM. Apple, Meta and Microsoft all sought roughly four times the amount.
Under the second Trump administration, at the direction of Vice President JD Vance , efforts have been made to address concerns about the H-1B visa and its green card pathway. One of the major concerns is that tech companies have laid off thousands of roles while still applying for visas.
In October, Vance announced Microsoft and a handful of other major companies would have their access to the PERM program suspended over alleged fraud.
"We want people to invest in the United States of America, particularly the American technology sector," Vance said during an October 8 press conference. "We are the biggest boosters of your industry. We want you to continue to grow and to employ a lot of people, but we want you to employ American workers."
Elsewhere, the Department of Justice has reached settlements with Instacart and Open AI over their alleged abuse of the PERM system , after the companies advertised roles in a way that appeared to favor foreign workers.
IBM has not been the focus of any public comments by the Trump administration on this issue so far.

articles.title_orig: Top UK appeals court rules gay sex not a crime in the Caribbean nation of Trinidad and Tobago
articles.title_zh: Top UK appeals court rules gay sex not a crime in the Caribbean nation of Trinidad and Tobago
articles.content_orig:
London’s Privy Council ruled in favour of Jason Jones, who said the Caribbean nation’s ‌Sexual Offences Act breached his human rights
Trinidad ⁠and Tobago’s law criminalising ⁠consensual sexual relations between ⁠male same-sex couples was overturned by a London court on Tuesday, after a legal challenge by a gay man who said the law breached his human rights.
Jason Jones challenged the Caribbean nation’s ‌Sexual Offences Act – which made “buggery” and “gross indecency” illegal – as breaching his fundamental rights under the country’s constitution.
London’s Privy Council, the final court of appeal for Trinidad and Tobago, ruled in Jones’ favour, saying it was unconstitutional for the law to “criminalise private, consensual sexual relations between adults of the same ⁠sex”.

articles.title_orig: PlayStation announces end of PC streaming in December
articles.title_zh: PlayStation announces end of PC streaming in December
articles.content_orig:
PlayStation is ending support for the PS Plus app for PC on December 10. This will block users from streaming their PlayStation games to their PC.
PlayStation quietly announced the move in a blog post going over the latest PS Plus offerings. Towards the end, PlayStation says that the PC app is being discontinued due to a lack of interest amongst players, claiming that less than 0.4% of PS Plus Premium members were using it.
“We wanted to let you know that from December 10, we will be retiring the PlayStation Plus app on PC,” the announcement opens.
“PlayStation believes in providing high-quality experiences to our players, and we regularly review offerings to ensure we are focusing on experiences our members value most. With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4%) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use. As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available.
“This change does not affect PlayStation Plus memberships or benefits available on PS5 and PS4 consoles. We appreciate everyone who used the app on PC and will be notifying affected users directly.”
This signals an end to being able to play PlayStation console-exclusive titles on PC through the streaming workaround. This feature will now be exclusive to Xbox , which does allow its users to play its games on different platforms (either through streaming, or natively through Play Anywhere).
It also comes as PlayStation has reversed its PC strategy, no longer porting many of its exclusives to PC after their PS5 launch.
This is just one way in which PlayStation is honing in on the most popular ways to play its games. Controversially, it is also ditching physical game releases by 2028 , going digital-only for any games released on its platforms.

articles.title_orig: Pixel Tag tidbits: Surprise NFC, Find Hub setup, & Bellroy keychain cases
articles.title_zh: Pixel Tag tidbits: Surprise NFC, Find Hub setup, & Bellroy keychain cases
articles.content_orig:
The Made by Google 2026 lineup is finally complete with tomorrow’s retail launch of the Pixel Tag . You can find our review here , while there are some additional details about the device since the August announcement.
The Pixel Tag is the first Find Hub tracker with NFC. Google did not mention this connectivity specification in August, with Near Field Communication letting you tap the tracker to the back of your phone to immediately open device settings. The NFC area on the Pixel Tag is below the circular battery door, which you hold down and twist counterclockwise to open.
On Android 17 QPR2, tapping immediately opens the details page. On QPR1, you first get a system notification that you need to click. NFC joins Bluetooth 6.0 with Channel Sounding and Ultra Wideband (UWB).
The setup process adds a new screen after the initial pairing and terms of use. It lets you configure: Notify when left behind, Ring this phone, Edit name, Edit category, and Adjust volume for this tag.
The Pixel Tag has a physical button on the rear side below the battery cover. Clicking twice plays a loud sound on your phone if both devices are nearby. Once found, you can tap the button once to silence, or turn it off from your phone. This feature can be disabled from the Pixel Tag’s device details page on a tracker-by-tracker basis.
Google does not have a first-party case for the Pixel Tag. Instead, it’s working with Made for Google partner Bellroy.
There are two models available from the Google Store, with the first made of silicone. The Bellroy Lite Case Duo costs $24.99 and comes in a pack of two: Mist and Shadow colorways. It wraps everything but the face of the Pixel Tag (and its speaker cutout), while giving you a hole in the corner and color-matching cord.
There’s also the Bellroy Leather Tag Case in Artichoke, Azalea, Black, Pewter, and Red Ochre for $29.99.

articles.title_orig: Google Pixel Tag Initial Review: The gold standard for Find Hub trackers, whatever that’s worth
articles.title_zh: Google Pixel Tag Initial Review: The gold standard for Find Hub trackers, whatever that’s worth
articles.content_orig:
Google’s Find Hub had a tumultuous launch for its performance , but also for a lack of clear direction in hardware. Over two years later, that’s finally arriving in the Google Pixel Tag which, even just a few days in, is the obvious gold standard in the race to build an AirTag for Android devices.
There are plenty of really good Android Find Hub trackers on the market. Pebblebee and Chipolo have been long-standing examples of how to build good dual-network trackers that work on both Android and iOS, while Motorola’s Moto Tag series has delivered two Android-only trackers that deliver better performance and more focused features. But even with the Moto Tag, there’s a clear compromise. Features like the ability to ring your phone are tied to a separate app and, in turn, have some inherent clunkiness.
Pixel Tag is the device that finally brings it all together, and it’s brilliant so far.
I’ve only had the Pixel Tag for a week and, frankly, it’s impossible to properly review a tracker in that time. There are only so many ways to artificially test out how a tracker works, as most cases where you’ll find value in this sort of product can only occur in real life.
So, with that said, let’s focus on the fundamentals.
Google Pixel Tag pairs to your Android phone just like any other Find Hub tracker – though much faster compared to some others I’ve tested – but the differences are obvious towards the end of that process. The final screen shows options for setting ringer volume and an option to set up “Ring this phone.”
Those new features are what make the Pixel Tag so good, and so appealing compared to all of the competition. A quick double-tap on the Tag’s button rings whichever phone you connected it to, assuming it’s in range, and it works pretty reliably. You can also set up “left behind” alerts (now available on other Find Hub trackers too) for when the phone leaves the tracker behind – you can set up exclusion zones such as your home or work address.
One of my favorite examples of the added polish from Google is the ability to adjust the ringer volume on the page where you actually want to ring the tracker. In a crowded but quiet space where you know the tracker is close by, being able to quickly set the volume to low is a great addition. In my book, it’s the reason to buy Pixel Tag over any other Android tracker.
UWB, of course, only makes up-close finding all the better. I found this decently reliable on my Pixel 11 Pro XL, but it is a little bit frustrating that the directional cues vanish within about 10-12 feet. Fine for a backpack or something like that, potentially a problem if your Tag is attached to a set of keys.
On that note, my biggest hardware complaint is that Google took the Apple route of having no built-in mounting mechanism. The super thin and light hardware of Pixel Tag is wonderful, don’t get me wrong, but being forced to buy a separate accessory just to attach it to my bag is frustrating! One of Google’s partners, Bellroy, built one of these accessories and it’s simple enough – a silicone case with a rope. I wish I didn’t need it, but it works, and at least you get two of them in a pack for $25.
The hardware itself is pretty good across the board, really, with the battery door also being slightly easier to open compared to the Moto Tag. Inside is a standard CR2032 battery that Google says will last “over one year.” I’d personally still prefer a rechargeable battery with USB-C or wireless charging, but this is a good enough solution given the amount of time the battery lasts – hopefully Google’s claim lives up.
Rounding out some of the key aspects here, it’s worth saying that the built-in speaker is more than loud enough at its highest setting, but the value for me so far has really come in that the low setting is actually low enough to not be a nuisance. I do find it a little strange that there’s no visual indication of where the Tag’s button is, but the packaging and app both do a good enough job of letting you know.
Overall performance in Find Hub seems fine, but as mentioned at the outset, this is a really hard thing to test artificially, all the more so in the span of just a few days. Google’s Find Hub network has gotten a lot better in the past two years, but it’s still hit or miss in my experience. It’s very clear that Google is making an effort to reverse the privacy-inspired decision to effectively disable the Find Hub network outside of crowded areas, but the damage has been done. I’m not sure the network will ever fully recover from that misstep, regardless of what tracker you’re using it with.
I’m looking forward to seeing how Pixel Tag performs as the travel season spins back up, so stay tuned for a later long-term review of Google’s tracker in the coming months. Initial impressions, though, are solid. Sound off in the comments below if you have any questions around Pixel Tag, I’ll answer everything I can!
If you’re interested in picking up a Pixel Tag, it’ll be available on November 11.

Stocks have continued to trade with a downward bias, especially semiconductor names.

articles.title_orig: The Culprit Behind Thousands of Ancient Frog Deaths Are Owls
articles.title_zh: The Culprit Behind Thousands of Ancient Frog Deaths Are Owls
articles.content_orig:
The culprits behind a massive frog cemetery that has baffled scientists have turned out to be a group of short-eared owls.
Between 2016 and 2018, 8,000 ancient frog bones were discovered in a single ditch near the site of an Iron Age roundhouse at Bar Hill, near Cambridge.
Scientists at Bournemouth University and Museum of London Archaeology (MOLA) have now identified that birds of prey were behind the 1,700 year-old cold case.
Dr Paul Clarkson, of Bournemouth University, said people "don't often get an owl's eye view of what it was like in the past from archaeological sites".
The researchers compared the damage to the frog bones to previous studies, finding they had most likely been eaten by short-eared owls and hen harriers.
Archaeological evidence also showed the ditch filled within a single year.
The university team used a new method of analysis to discover that most of the frogs died young, having been eaten in the winter of their first year of life.
Radiocarbon dating by the University of Vienna also showed the remains dated back 1,700 years to Roman period.
The fen wetlands were retreating in the valley in the Roman period, creating ideal conditions for the frogs to breed in.
Large areas of woodland were gradually felled over time for grazing livestock, which then left the amphibians with fewer trees to protect them from the grassland hunters.
Clarkson said the solution to the mystery was "a feast of frogs that were eaten and their bones left behind by a group of owls".
"These bones not only tell us about life for people living near the Roman Fens, but they also give insights into the natural world - what wild animals were getting up to in the past, and what life was like for them," he said.
Senior zooarchaeologist Dr Vicki Ewens said she had "so many theories" before the solution was found.
She said the research showed "how even the smallest animal recovered on a site can help us to understand not only past environmental conditions but human activity within a wider landscape".

articles.title_orig: We moved to Sweden for my husband's job 4 years ago. Now, we're struggling to keep the life we worked so hard to build.
articles.title_zh: We moved to Sweden for my husband's job 4 years ago. Now, we're struggling to keep the life we worked so hard to build.
articles.content_orig:
I've never had a problem with commitment.
I got married at 18, and our relationship is still going strong 23 years later. Ten years ago, I started my own business and never looked back.
When something feels right, I don't waste time keeping my options open. I go all in. So when my husband, Jarrod, got a video-game development job in Sweden in 2022, we committed.
We bought a home, enrolled our son in school, registered my business, and started learning the language. We made friends, shopped local, and got Swedish driver's licenses.
Unfortunately, none of that matters much when your visa is tied to an employer.
To be clear, uprooting our lives to live in another country wasn't a willy-nilly decision.
Before agreeing to the job and the move, we visited Skövde in person and met with several founding members of Jarrod's prospective studio. It seemed as well-managed and stable as any game studio can be, and Jarrod was excited to jump into the role as art director.
Plus, there were several other video-game studios in town. Video games can be a fickle business, and this meant there could be other local employment opportunities if something went sideways.
We also checked out the schools and the housing market. We ended up buying a great home on Billingen Mountain.
Add BI in Google so our reporting is easier to find when you’re searching for what matters.
It's big enough for two home offices, a playroom, and a guest room for our American family and friends — but with a small yard, so the maintenance isn't overwhelming.
The yard even has an apple tree with a swing that's the perfect size for our son, and he stops to play on it every day when he gets home from school.
As much as we missed our friends and family back in the US, we spent the next few years settling into a lovely life in Sweden .
We continued practicing the language and building community — and got very accustomed to the affordable childcare and accessible healthcare.
We adapted to the seasons and local quirks, too. I created a sunset coffee routine to survive the winter when the sun sets shortly after 3 p.m. And I bought blackout curtains for when the sun sets after 10 p.m. in the summer.
Sweden truly became our home; a place we could imagine living in for the long haul.
A few years later, when Jarrod's studio closed with little warning, we were reminded that our life here was contingent on that job.
As Americans here on a work visa , even homeownership doesn't grant us the right to stay in Sweden. And with his particular permit, Jarrod was given three months to find a comparable position or leave the country.
Unfortunately, the economy has shifted since we created our contingency plan. A large percentage of local game studios had closed, and none of the remaining ones had art-director positions available.
So, Jarrod's job search extended to surrounding cities, like Gothenburg and Stockholm.
Unfortunately, finding another position in an already struggling industry has proven harder than we'd anticipated. Plus, hiring a non-citizen feels like a big ask because of the bureaucratic red tape and costs that can come with it.
Thankfully, my business earns enough to cover our expenses. So even before Jarrod's job search began, I contacted the Swedish Migration Agency office to let them know we are self-sufficient.
Meanwhile, Jarrod began working with several former colleagues to launch a new game studio, creating their own employment opportunities in an industry where jobs were disappearing.
However, until the studio can pay him a salary, that work doesn't qualify as employment for immigration purposes. Ultimately, the agency has asked us to leave, and we have formally appealed that decision.
I began wondering if it was naive of me to think we could build a life in Sweden — maybe even entitled.
We'd come here legally, paid taxes, learned the language, and bought a property. It was frustrating to feel like all of the ways we've integrated into the country over the past years didn't seem to matter.
For now, I'm continuing to run my business in Sweden ; my husband is trying to build his; and we're working through the appeal process with the help of our local attorney to see if we can remain here.
Each time I check the mail, I hold my breath. Best-case scenario: I get notified that our visa has been renewed for two more years. Worst-case scenario: I find a notice of denial and a legal demand that we leave by a certain date. Most likely scenario: our Telia phone bill.
Despite everything, I don't think the lesson here is to live with reservations moving forward. Committing less wouldn't have made the last four years any better.
I don't know whether we'll get to stay in this country — but I do know that when our son gets home from school tomorrow, he's going to stop for a swing under our apple tree.
And even if our time here ends up being temporary, buying a home and assimilating to life in Sweden has been an unforgettable adventure for all of us.

articles.title_orig: 10 PS Plus Extra, Premium Games for November 2026 Announced
articles.title_zh: 10 PS Plus Extra, Premium Games for November 2026 Announced
articles.content_orig:
Soul Reaver 2 and Freedom Wars  Remastered join PlayStation Plus Premium.
This month, embark on an inspiring mission of human connection in Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, assemble a one-of-a-kind crew as you explore the open sea in Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii, navigate the cult-controlled ruins, natural caves, and nuclear bunkers of a green and unpleasant British countryside in Atomfall, or explore a vast world map with an abundance of captivating locations in Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake. All these titles and more are available in November’s PlayStation Plus Game Catalog lineup*. Meanwhile, Soul Reaver 2 and Freedom Wars Remastered land into PlayStation Plus Premium. The full lineup will be available to play from November 17, unless otherwise noted.
Death Stranding 2: On the Beach | PS5
Embark on an inspiring mission of human connection beyond the UCA. Join Sam for the next chapter of his journey as he attempts to connect Australia to the Chiral Network. Navigate a living environment through day and night cycles, natural disasters including earthquakes, sandstorms and forest fires, and Timefall – a rain that instantly ages everything it touches. To traverse this dangerous landscape, you’ll need to build new types of infrastructure, master specialised equipment, and confront (or evade) the otherworldly creatures that roam the fractured world.
Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii | PS5, PS4
A new legend begins as you step into the steel toe boots of Goro Majima, a man who has lost his memory and reinvents himself as a pirate on the open sea. Embark on an over-the-top, modern-day pirate adventure with an ex-yakuza, now pirate captain and his crew as they engage in exhilarating combat on land and sea in the hunt for lost memories and a legendary treasure.
Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii will be available November 24 in the US, the UK and Japan.
A survival-action game inspired by real-life events, Atomfall is set five years after the Windscale nuclear disaster in Northern England. Explore the fictional quarantine zone, scavenge, craft, barter, fight and talk your way through a British countryside setting filled with bizarre characters, mysticism, cults, and rogue government agencies. From Rebellion, the studio behind Sniper Elite and Zombie Army, Atomfall will challenge you to solve the dark mystery of what really happened.
Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake | PS5
A stunning reimagining of the beloved RPG masterpiece and narrative beginning to The Erdrick Trilogy. Years ago, the great hero Ortega bid farewell to his wife and child as he set off on a quest to defeat the villainous Archfiend, Baramos. Ortega failed his quest, and Baramos still threatens the world. Now, on their 16th birthday, Ortega’s only child is summoned by the king of Aliahan and entrusted with a mission of the highest import: to take on Ortega’s quest, vanquish Baramos and save the world.
In Trepang2, you play as an escaped soldier who has no memories of their past life, but is infused with supernatural abilities. Revenge is on your mind, and you’ll stop at nothing to get what you want. Deliver devastating punches, sneak around in the shadows, wield explosive weapons, and give the bad guys a taste of their own medicine. Fight back, find the truth and face a threat even deadlier than yourself.
Trepang2 will be available November 24 in the US and the UK.
Experience the full intensity of the 2026 MotoGP Championship with all the official riders, teams, bikes and tracks in a more authentic way: for the first time, the real-world results dynamically update Riders Ratings, directly influencing in-game performance throughout the season. Step into the spotlight and track your journey with dazzling Collectible Cards celebrating your progress.
MotoGP 26 will be available November 24 in the US and the UK.
Join the ever-expanding experience of Hell Let Loose – a hardcore World War Two first person shooter with epic battles of 100 players with infantry, tanks, artillery, a dynamically shifting front line and a unique resource based RTS-inspired meta-game. Take to the battlefield in 50 vs 50 multiplayer across huge maps. Choose one of 14 playable roles within infantry, recon and armour unit types, each equipped with different weapons, vehicles and equipment. Play as an Officer, Scout, Machine Gunner, Medic, Engineer, Tank Commander and more to experience every aspect of World War II combat.
Hell Let Loose will be available tomorrow, November 11 in the US, the UK and November 12 in Japan.
Cricket 26 – The Official Game of the Ashes | PS5, PS4
Featuring the all-new Management Career, a bigger and better Pro Team, in-depth Ashes mode, and expanded control on and off the field from enhanced gameplay and in-depth strategies – Cricket 26 is The Ultimate Showdown.
Cricket 26 – The Official Game of the Ashes will be available November 24 in the US and the UK.
Soul Reaver 2 | PS5, PS4 In this sequel to the critically acclaimed Legacy of Kain: Soul Reaver, reassume the role of Raziel, and battle back through the currents of time into pivotal, dangerous eras of Nosgoth’s past in your relentless pursuit of Kain. Encounter new enemies as you unearth the mysteries of Nosgoth’s ancient races, and expose the schemes that lie behind the corruption of the Pillars.
Freedom Wars Remastered | PS5, PS4
In a distant future where all resources on earth have been depleted, being alive is a sin by itself. Born into a one-million-year prison sentence, you must survive deadly missions to earn any hope of freedom. Die in prison or live on the battlefield. The choice is yours. Use your most trusted weapon, your Thorn, to dominate the battlefield. Stand alongside your allies and your warden cyborg Accessory to face off against powerful enemies.
*PlayStation Plus Game Catalog and PlayStation Plus Premium/Deluxe lineups may differ by region. Please check PlayStation Store on release day. Digital PS5 games available to stream from your library will vary over time, region, and country.
We wanted to let you know that from December 10, we will be retiring the PlayStation Plus app on PC.
PlayStation believes in providing high-quality experiences to our players, and we regularly review offerings to ensure we are focusing on experiences our members value most. With a very small number of eligible PlayStation Plus Premium members (less than 0.4%) using the PlayStation Plus app on PC, making this change allows us to focus on enhancing high-quality experiences that more of our members want to use. As a result, the PlayStation Plus cloud streaming app on PC will no longer be available.
This change does not affect PlayStation Plus memberships or benefits available on PS5 and PS4 consoles. We appreciate everyone who used the app on PC and will be notifying affected users directly.

articles.title_orig: Singapore seizes US-operated cruise ship that offered ‘permanent’ life at sea
articles.title_zh: Singapore seizes US-operated cruise ship that offered ‘permanent’ life at sea
articles.content_orig:
MV Odyssey impounded by authorities almost a fortnight after passengers left stranded in Cambodian port
Singapore has seized a US-operated cruise ship that offered retirees a “permanent” life at sea but instead offloaded them in Cambodia after it ran out of money due to soaring fuel prices.
After more than 200 passengers were left stranded in the Cambodian port city of Sihanoukville last month , the MV Odyssey sailed on to ⁠Singapore last week and has been impounded by authorities.
“The vessel has been placed under arrest ⁠pursuant to a court order,” Singapore’s Maritime and Port ​Authority said in ‌a statement. “The crew onboard ‌are reported to be well and arrangements for their ‌welfare and wellbeing are being managed by the vessel’s creditors. There are no passengers on board.”
According to court records , ​the MV Odyssey was listed “under sheriff’s arrest” on Sunday morning ​just off Singapore’s east coast, meaning it had been detained but was not necessarily under any criminal charges.
It was not clear why the ship had been impounded, although Singapore is a global shipping hub, and it is not unusual for ships facing commercial issues to relocate to the city-state to resolve disputes.
The local Straits Times reported that the ship’s Florida-based operator, Villa Vie Residences, owed approximately US$500,000 in fuel payments . Villa Vie Residences has been contacted for comment.
On 27 October, and with only a few hours’ notice, the company disembarked all passengers , saying fuel ⁠price surges from the Iran war had made operations ​“unsustainable”. Mikael Petterson, the founder ‌and executive chair of Villa Vie Residences, later said the ship was now being operated by creditors.
Most of the passengers of the MV Odyssey were Americans, along with 156 crew members, Cambodian officials said.
Passengers were sold what the company website said was “a new model of global living at sea”, with the 195-metre (640-ft) vessel offering multi-year residencies as well as permanent cabin costs between $120,000 (£90,000) and $440,000. However, monthly fuel cost per cabin in parts of Asia has risen to as much as $8,000 from $1,800, the company said in a statement.
Some passengers have stayed in Cambodia to assess their options, including Lanette Canen and Johan Bodin, who had been documenting their life at sea on YouTube. In a video published last week and filmed on a beach with the Odyssey in the background, the couple said the “bank” was now making a decision on its fate. They later filmed the ship leaving at night.
The round-the-world cruise faced issues from the start, including a four-month delay in setting sail from Belfast, Northern Ireland, in October 2024. Several passengers reported signs of financial distress during the cruise, including accounts of guests raising extra money for fuel.
Randy Cassingham, a writer living onboard the ship, said after passengers were off-loaded, residents had also passed a jar around to raise $100 each for lower-ranking crew. He said few passengers expected to recover any of the funds they had spent on their cabins, as they knew the company had “been in terrible money problems from the beginning”.

articles.title_orig: Chinese Israel envoy rejects claims Beijing provides military assistance to Iran
articles.title_zh: Chinese Israel envoy rejects claims Beijing provides military assistance to Iran
articles.content_orig:
Shelves were left bare by the cyber-attacks
Iran has described French accusations that it was behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers as "baseless and hostile".
On Monday, the French authorities blamed Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) for the string of hacks, which foreign minister Jean-NoÃ«l Barrot said were "unprecedented" in terms of their scale and "level of aggression".
He added that those responsible would be hit with sanctions.
The French cyber-attacks, which led to the destruction of tons of frozen and chilled food, were followed by a similar hacks against supermarkets across several other European countries. It is not known if the instances are linked.
Barrot said the attack on France's supermarkets "marks the first large-scale cyber-attack aimed at sabotage on our national territory, and it constitutes a major attack on the nation's interests and the security of the French people".
He said the government had summoned the Iranian ambassador to Paris to "lodge a very strong protest against this extremely grave act".
France will take "any other necessary and proportionate measures" to respond to the incident and "deter anyone who might seek to repeat it", Barrot added.
The Paris prosecutor, Laure Beccuau, said an investigation had been opened into the head of an offensive cyber unit associated with the IRGC as well as his two deputies.
Beccuau named the unit as Shahid Kaveh, which she said had an affiliation with the electronic and cyber centre of the IRGC.
Shahid Kaveh is the name given to a cluster of hackers thought to be directly employed by the Iranian regime.
In recent weeks, a number of commentators and politicians in Iran have argued that the country should extend any retaliation beyond the Middle East if the US and Israel resume the war they started earlier this year.
On Monday, some Iranian media outlets denied the French accusations, but there had been no official comment until Tuesday's statement from Iran's foreign ministry.
On 11 October, hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units used in many of France's supermarkets.
More than 100 of CoopÃ©rative U's supermarkets were hit, as well as 180 stores from IntermarchÃ© and its Netto brand. In some stores, temperatures of the fridges reportedly rose to 50C (120F) overnight.
Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss.
The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely.
Earlier this month a second wave of hacks took place, hitting more than 100 stores across Europe.
Supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in countries including Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.
Separately in August a small number of US military bases had fridges mysteriously malfunction, spoiling food. This incident is also being investigated as deliberate cyber-attacks, Reuters news agency has reported, citing sources familiar with the matter.
Since the waves of attacks on freezers, experts have been speculating which hacking groups could be responsible, with Iran being on a list of potential suspects.
In spite of a pair of Russian-aligned hacktivist groups claiming they were responsible on Wednesday, few believed them.
The French government has not said how it reached the conclusion that Iran was responsible, and attribution of cyber-attacks is extremely hard as hackers are able to hide their locations.
Additional reporting by Farshad Bayan, BBC Persian.

articles.title_orig: U.S. gas prices fall below $4 for the first time since July
articles.title_zh: U.S. gas prices fall below $4 for the first time since July
articles.content_orig:
Americans may finally find some relief at the pump.
The national average price of regular gasoline fell below $4 a gallon for the first time since July, reaching $3.9788 on Tuesday, according to AAA . Prices are down about 17 cents from a week ago and nearly 39 cents from a month ago.
The decline comes after energy inflation slowed significantly in October. Energy prices increased 0.7% during the month, a far cry from the 5.2% surge seen in September, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics . The BLS' gasoline index increased 1% over the month, after advancing 9.1% in September.
Bespoke Investment Group pointed out that gasoline prices also tend to decline at this time of the year, making part of the recent relief seasonal.
"While lower oil prices have been a tailwind for the relief at the pump, it's also perfectly normal for gas prices to be falling at this time of year, so if they weren't, there would really be something wrong," the firm said.
The drop at the pump followed a sharp retreat in crude oil. International oil benchmark Brent crude on Tuesday briefly fell below $90 a barrel for the first time since August as comments from U.S. President Donald Trump fueled hopes for an end to Washington's nearly nine-month conflict with Iran.
Recovering oil flows from the Persian Gulf have also eased supply concerns. Regional crude exports have returned to an estimated 80% to 85% of prewar levels, including pipeline shipments, according to ING .
"Energy markets remain under pressure as hopes for a de-escalation in the Middle East reduce geopolitical risk premiums. Oil extended its losses as Gulf supply flows continued to recover, while European gas also moved lower," analysts at ING wrote.
However, the Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller warned Tuesday that energy shocks may have more persistent effects on inflation than they did before the pandemic.
"While I am pleased to see energy prices down from their high rates over the past week or so, they are still quite elevated relative to the start of the year, and the ultimate effect on inflation will depend on what levels are sustained," he said.
