articles.title_orig: Amazon’s Ring debuts security robots including a drone
articles.title_zh: Amazon’s Ring debuts security robots including a drone
articles.content_orig:
Amazon’s Ring has launched an indoor security drone , the company said Tuesday, offering homeowners room-to-room surveillance where a fixed camera cannot reach.
The $250 Ring Drone Camera offers exactly what the product’s name implies — the technology to capture moving images from a lens affixed to a small quadcopter drone, according to the company .
Ring founder and chief inventor Jamie Siminoff said his customers have been asking for an expansion of the company’s popular doorbell cameras without having to install more cameras around the house.
“For years, customers told us they wanted eyes in the places a fixed camera couldn’t reach, and peace of mind in the spots they’d never want one,” Siminoff said in a statement released by the company Tuesday.
“The honest answer wasn’t more cameras; it meant reimagining what a security device could be. That kind of invention is hard, and it takes time. But we kept at it until we got it right—and that’s Ring Robotics. It’s not just a new category of security; it’s the beginning of a future where proactive, autonomous protection is something every home and every business can have.”
The drone provides “wall-to-wall coverage,” according to Ring, with 148-degree peripheral vision and the ability to rotate 360 degrees to quickly spot potential threats.
LED lights also equip it to work in “low-light environments” so that homeowners can “always get clear, crisp video,” the company said.
Ring also rolled out its  $1,000 Ring Rover Cam, tailored for businesses.
The tool could be used to “investigate a disturbance” or be set  to do “regular sweeps” of the property.
“Get a closer look wherever and whenever you need it without the cost and complexity of wiring up every corner of every room,” the company said.
Both pieces of equipment require a subscription fee of $5 per month or $60 annually, a customer service rep told NBC News.

articles.title_orig: iPadOS 27.3 adds new iPad setting I instantly turned on
articles.title_zh: iPadOS 27.3 adds new iPad setting I instantly turned on
articles.content_orig:
iPadOS 27.3 is currently available in beta , and it introduces a new iPad setting for app windowing that I instantly turned on. Here are the details.
I use the iPad Pro as my primary computer, and for the most part have found Apple’s software changes in iPadOS 26 and 27 to be great upgrades.
But with the powerful new windowing capabilities, there have definitely been some quirks that need refining. One of them involves resizing windows with the traffic light controls in the top-left corner.
For example, in iPadOS 27 the controls move locations and even disappear depending on the size of the window. It can be pretty frustrating.
I need to just get better about learning keyboard shortcuts for window controls. But in the meantime, iPadOS 27.3 adds a new optional setting that I instantly turned on and have been loving.
Inside Settings ⇾ Multitasking & Gestures, if you have ‘Windowed Apps’ enabled you’ll see a new option below it: ‘Double-tap Top of Window to Zoom’
If you use your iPad mostly with touch input, or simply haven’t used keyboard shortcuts enough to remember them, this new setting is a great way to quickly resize windows.
When the setting is enabled, two taps (or a double-click with the trackpad) will zoom the window to take up the full screen. Then you can double-tap again to revert it to its previous size.
I generally keep my app windows in specific size setups, but regularly find myself wanting to go fullscreen temporarily. The new setting provides a convenient way to do that quickly without needing the traffic light controls or my keyboard, and is a welcome refinement to iPadOS windowing.
Will you enable this new iPadOS 27.3 setting? Why or why not? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title_orig: Stocks, Bonds Fall as CPI Data Fuel Fed-Hike Bets: Markets Wrap
articles.title_zh: Stocks, Bonds Fall as CPI Data Fuel Fed-Hike Bets: Markets Wrap
articles.content_orig:
Stocks fell on Tuesday after October inflation data came in hotter than expected and a key Federal Reserve official hinted at the possibility of a half-point rise in rates next month.
The S&P 500 traded down 0.9%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 302 points, or 0.6%. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.6%.
Nvidia dragged down the three major averages, falling 6%. The stock sat out Monday's tech-fueled rally following CEO Jensen Huang's admission over the weekend to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy .
The consumer price index rose 0.4% in October, above the gain of 0.3% that economists polled by Dow Jones expected. Core CPI — which excludes volatile food and energy costs — increased 0.3% in October, whereas economists had called for a 0.2% advance. Annual figures were not be provided for Tuesday's report because of the 2025 government shutdown.
Treasury yields jumped as traders reacted to the report, fearing that interest rate increases could now be more likely in 2027. The 10-year Treasury note yield in particular advanced back above 5% .
Earlier Tuesday, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech in London that he thinks a December rate hike is likely and opened the door for a possible half-point increase amid persistent  inflationary pressures.
"While the precise timing of the hikes doesn't matter, ensuring that the promised hikes are implemented in a reasonable period of time does," he said.
Traders now see a December rate hike as a near certainty and a small chance of a supersized increase. They also expect at least a quarter-point hike at some point next year.
"There's an extrapolation that maybe the Fed's going to have to hike rates more aggressively next year," said Tom Hainlin, national investment strategist at U.S. Bank Asset Management. He later added, "The CPI print said perhaps inflation is going to be a little stickier for a little longer."
Tuesday's retreat came one day after the S&P 500 posted its best day since April. The push and pull come after a rocky week for markets, in which traders grew concerned about the potential for a slowdown in data center buildouts after Democrats posted big victories in the midterm elections.
Check out CNBC's live blog to read more about the stocks making midday moves here .
— John Melloy, Deena Zaidi and Darla Mercado
Nike is hosting its first Investor Day since 2017 next week under a new management team led by CEO Elliott Hill.
The event could serve as a crucial moment for the company that has been struggling to turn its business around.

articles.title_orig: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature
articles.title_zh: Google releases Gemini 4 Carbon with agent ‘swarm’ feature
articles.content_orig:
It ‘pushes the frontier even further’ than its last release, Argon.﻿
It ‘pushes the frontier even further’ than its last release, Argon.﻿
Google is rolling out its latest AI model, Gemini 4 Carbon, to the general public after releasing it to a select group of “cybersecurity defenders” two weeks ago. Google claims Carbon is its “strongest model” yet, and capable of competing with the very best systems from Anthropic and OpenAI.
Google says Gemini 4 Carbon “pushes the frontier even further” than Argon, referring to the company’s other frontier model that launched only last month . The company said Argon will likely remain “the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work,” but that Carbon is “built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence,” such as complex, multi-step coding and open-ended scientific research.
To highlight Carbon’s utility for long-horizon work involving AI agents, Google said it is also previewing a “swarm” feature on its agentic development platform Antigravity, which will let users turn a single prompt “into a coordinated team of agents.”
Carbon is rolling out today via the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and Gemini for business for all paying developers and enterprises, Google said in a blog post. It will also be available to all Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, the AI Mode in Search, and on Antigravity. It is not clear when — or if — Carbon will be available to lower tier subscribers or free users.
As with the launch of Argon, Google is pricing Carbon very competitively. The model is launching with an introductory price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, around a fifth the cost of OpenAI’s GPT-6 Astra and a quarter the cost of Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 model, which launched yesterday . Even after those costs double at the end November — when the introductory period of lower prices finishes — Carbon will still be significantly cheaper than frontier rivals on a per-token basis, though this doesn’t necessarily translate to lower costs as models can use different numbers of tokens for the same tasks.
Benchmarks cited by Google when it first announced Carbon suggest the model is one of the most powerful on the market across most metrics, behind Fable 5.2. It should be noted that companies can and do cherry-pick benchmark results to show their tools in the best possible light.
The release, hot on the heels of Argon, marks a decisive return for Google at the very forefront of AI research . For months, frontier development looked like a two-horse race between Anthropic and OpenAI.

articles.title_orig: Meta’s AI agent Muse lands on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS
articles.title_zh: Meta’s AI agent Muse lands on Apple Watch and Android Wear OS
articles.content_orig:
Meta is bringing its Muse AI agent to the Apple Watch and Android’s Wear OS, the company announced on Monday. With the launch, users can now interact with Meta’s AI assistant through voice calls, text messages, or dictation directly on their smartwatch.
Works around the clock, and now on your wrist. Muse is now on Apple Watch and Wear OS ⌚️ pic.twitter.com/97QRap5XKz
The smartwatch launch comes just a month after Meta introduced a dedicated iPad app for Muse. First launched on the App Store in September, the AI assistant’s expansion across Apple devices signals Meta’s growing ambitions for its consumer AI product and its focus on making Muse a central part of its ecosystem.
Muse is now one of dozens of consumer-facing AI agents competing for users’ attention. Like many of its competitors, it allows users to connect their accounts to manage email, meetings, bills, and more, while also handling tasks such as booking reservations, ordering groceries, setting goals, and making purchases.
Users can also personalize their Muse avatar to their liking and change it into something that resembles a person, an animal, or another type of character.
Despite being a relatively new product, Meta has wasted little time introducing new capabilities to Muse.
A few days ago, Meta launched Spaces , a new way to communicate and collaborate with Muse. Spaces function as dedicated conversations around specific topics, which Meta describes as “custom experiences” as they’re mini apps that are built on the fly. They appear in the sidebar of the Muse interface and bring up a focused conversation where the AI agent works toward a particular goal on the user’s behalf.
Last week, Meta rolled out the ability for users in the U.S. to video chat with their Muse AI avatar. Meta said Muse will use “subtle expressions and gestures” that reflect the tone and context of the conversation as it speaks. It’s worth noting that Muse doesn’t actually see users, but can hear them and respond in real time.
Shortly after its launch, Muse became one of just 12 mobile apps to have surpassed 10 million U.S. downloads within their first 40 days in the App Store. Only 11 other apps have achieved this milestone, with Meta’s Threads being the most recent in July 2023.

articles.title_orig: Board of Peace says Israel's aid response after Gaza floods 'insufficent'
articles.title_zh: Board of Peace says Israel's aid response after Gaza floods 'insufficent'
articles.content_orig:
US President Donald Trump's Board of Peace has called on Israel to immediately allow all necessary humanitarian supplies into Gaza after rain flooded tens of thousands of tents.
The US-backed body, established to oversee the implementation of Trump's Gaza peace plan, acknowledged the steps now being considered by Israel, but said "the response remains insufficient".
Israel's military agency in charge of co-ordinating aid into Gaza said it had allowed in tens of thousands of tents and trucks with winter supplies, but added reconstruction "can only begin after Hamas fully disarms".
On Sunday, three children and a woman were killed when a sand embankment collapsed onto tents in the central Strip.
Most people in Gaza have been displaced because of Israel's military actions. Around 65% of the population, about 1.4 million people, now live in tents or makeshift shelters, the UN says.
Standing soaked in Gaza City, Mohammed Jneid told the AFP news agency that heavy rains hit from one side and sewage overflowed on them from the other, with the ground and tents no longer able to hold.
"We have nothing left, no bedding, no food, nothing," he said.
Sitting inside her tent, Islam Al Mobayed told AFP there were seven children there, five of them young.
"This is not life," she said. "We are exhausted, we are tired of this entire life."
In rare criticism of Israel, the Board of Peace said it had been urging the Israeli government to authorise the entry of essential goods for temporary shelter and water and sanitation infrastructure.
The Board added that delays in approving the entry of supplies "exacerbated the consequences of a foreseeable humanitarian challenge" and delayed the start of decommissioning weapons and transferring Hamas authority to a transitional government.
It also said Hamas's failure to disarm and transfer power had compounded the difficulties facing Gaza's civilians.
The UN's humanitarian agency OCHA said more than 150,000 tents were outside Gaza ready to go in, but aid efforts were constrained "by Israeli restrictions on the entry of supplies and equipment and funding shortfalls".
UN humanitarian coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov said on Monday that stocks of essential shelter and winter items inside Gaza had been exhausted.
"Israeli authorities must immediately lift all restrictions on entry of the supplies," he said, adding "we have run out of time".
Israel's foreign ministry spokeswoman Michal Maayan on Monday said Israel had in recent months put in place a winter plan in coordination with the Board of Peace and international charities.
That plan has brought in more than 91,000 tents and 8,200-plus trucks with tarpaulins, blankets, winter clothing, and other equipment, according to Cogat, the Israeli military body responsible for aid.
Cogat said it would not allow in equipment that could be used for military purposes.
Maayon accused Hamas of hoarding aid, saying: "Hamas is responsible for the delays in making more progress in the Strip, and winter-related hardships are a consequence of Hamas's action and policy."
In response to the Board of Peace, Hamas said in a statement published on Palestinian media that its comment "presents a distorted account of the causes of the disaster". The group denied it was responsible for ceasefire delays, pointing to a statement in August from Egyptian, Qatari and Turkish mediators that accused Israel of violations.
Hamas said Israeli restrictions prevent the entry of materials necessary for shelter and recovery - and added the Board as the ceasefire implementor should look at its own "serious shortcoming".
Under the deal to end the two-year-long war in October 2025, Hamas agreed to give up governance and its weapons in exchange for a phased Israeli troop withdrawal from the 60% of Gaza it still occupied. Israel, however, has insisted Hamas must fully disarm before withdrawal.
The dispute has left the next stages of the peace plan stalled, with both sides blaming each other.
The war in Gaza began after the Hamas-led attack on Israel on 7 October 2023 when around 1,200 people were killed and 251 others taken hostage.
The Israeli military campaign in response has killed 74,645 people, according to the Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures the UN considers reliable. More than 1,600 people have been killed since the ceasefire in October last year.
Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza since then.

articles.title_zh: Galaxy S27 redesign leak shows off Pro vs Ultra size difference, with just a bit of controversy
articles.content_orig:
Samsung is working on a long overdue redesign for its Galaxy S27 series and, this week, we’re getting a fresh look.
We’ve already seen it in renders, but leaker Sonny Dickson took to Twitter/X today to present an image of Galaxy S27 Pro, Ultra, and S27+ dummy units, and it tells us a few things.
First, we get to see the redesign again, this time in “real life.” That’s, of course, with the caveat that these aren’t real devices, and probably aren’t reflective of the final design either. The Pro and Ultra both have a full-width camera island akin to Apple’s latest iPhone design language, and a big departure from the vertical camera array that Samsung insisted was its “core identity” mere months ago.
Importantly, we can also see the size difference between Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro, with the Pro being noticeably smaller compared to both the Ultra and the S27+. For small(er) phone fans, it’s looking great .
All of that said, adding a bit of controversy to this image is leaker Ice Universe, who says “this picture is wrong.”
Ice points out that the Galaxy S27 Ultra and Pro both do not have a fourth camera lens, which is correct based on recent leaks . That said, it’s not much of a leap to assume these dummy units are based on an older design, or are confusing a sensor. After all, these are mainly used to test accessories and, this early on, there’s plenty of room for inaccuracy.

US stocks slipped Tuesday as investors digested a hotter-than-expected inflation report that cemented bets that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 0.6%, while the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) gave back 0.8% in gains and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) tumbled 1.4%. The moves in major indices come after a sharp rally in US stocks on Monday.
The Consumer Price Index , released on Tuesday morning, showed prices rose 0.4% in October from a month earlier, higher than the 0.3% economists were expecting but cooler than September's 0.6% gain. October's CPI report did not include annual inflation figures because last year's government shutdown limited the data available.
Traders now overwhelmingly expect the Fed to hike interest rates by 25 basis points, with a subset of Fed watchers expecting a 50 basis point jumbo hike. Recent comments by Fed governor Chris Waller reinforced those bets , as he noted he would be open to a larger hike.
Nvidia ( NVDA ) investors continue to reel from the board's investigation into CEO Jensen Huang following reports of his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia stock continued to edge lower on Tuesday morning after falling over 4% the day before.
In other tech news, Anthropic began its roadshow and released an updated filing ahead of its highly anticipated IPO . The AI lab is forging ahead with its public debut despite recent volatility in tech stocks, and is seeking a valuation of $1.4 trillion.
Oil prices are falling, with Brent crude ( BZ=F ), the international benchmark, and WTI crude ( CL=F ), the US benchmark, declining by around 3%.
While most of the third quarter earnings season is in the rearview mirror, Nvidia-backed neocloud CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and quantum computing stocks Quantum ( QBTS ) and Rigetti Computing ( RGTI ) report results after the bell today.

US stocks moved lower Tuesday following a hotter-than-expected inflation report that cemented bets that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates next month.
The move has strengthened the US dollar and sent US Treasury yields higher, a setup that has proved difficult for bitcoin's price in recent months, according to Lewis Huang, an analyst for crypto exchange Bitget.
Bitcoin slipped below its 200-day moving average of $73,200 by Tuesday at noon New York time. Dropping below the key support level "could increase the risk of a deeper pullback," Huang added.
Investors are also grappling with a reset in tech stock valuations amid a volatile stretch for artificial intelligence-related names.
Crypto-related stocks also fell Tuesday. Shares of Coinbase Global ( COIN ) and Michael Saylor's Strategy ( MSTR ) both fell 4%, while Robinhood ( HOOD ) shares declined more than 3%.

"Even in a 'no growth' scenario for 2028 (which we see as relatively unlikely), NVDA/AVGO are trading 12X/13X this baseline — which we believe valuations are compelling at current levels," Schneider wrote in a note. "We find AMD to be very attractive given the growth we believe it can achieve, albeit at a less compelling valuation."

The stock came under pressure amid a broader market sell-off and growing concerns about increased scrutiny of the chipmaker following CEO Jensen Huang's admission to an affair believed to involve a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy, Yahoo Finance's Ines Ferré has the latest:
The scrutiny could center on Megaspeed, the Singapore-based company where Alice Huang previously worked, and on whether she helped divert restricted Nvidia chips to China. The Information reported Tuesday that at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia hardware had been shipped to Chinese companies through a network linked to Alice Huang since 2023, citing two people who knew her.
On Monday, US House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries said Congress needs more answers about the matter, adding that there are "real ⁠concerns that need to be addressed with respect to the ​Nvidia situation."
US stocks opened lower on Tuesday after hotter-than-expected inflation data strengthened expectations for another Federal Reserve rate hike in December.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average ( ^DJI ) fell 0.2%, while those on the S&P 500 ( ^GSPC ) fell 0.5%. The Nasdaq Composite ( ^IXIC ) dropped 0.8% after stocks rallied on Monday.
Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October from the prior month, above economists' expectations for a 0.3% increase. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, rose 0.3%, also hotter than forecast.
The report pushed Treasury yields higher, strengthening bets on another Fed rate hike in December. The move comes after stocks saw a sharp stock rally on Monday as oil prices continued to fall.
Shorter-term Treasury yields jumped sharply after the CPI inflation data was released, keeping the pressure on the Fed to raise rates at its next meeting.
The 5-year yield ( ^FVX ) jumped 10 basis points to 4.75%, while the 10-year Treasury yield rose 7 basis points to 4.93%. The 30-year yield ( ^TYX ) increased 3 basis points to 5.29%.
Traders now see an 84% chance that the Fed will raise interest rates by 25 basis points in December. Bets that the Fed will hike by 50 basis points jumped from 0% yesterday to 15% today.
The move comes after Fed governor Chris Waller said he would be open to a jumbo 50 basis point rate hike in December if inflation came in hot.
"Inflation is too high … this means that even if, as I expect, the monthly rate of inflation improves in October, I am leaning toward supporting an increase in our policy rate of 25 basis points at the FOMC's December meeting," Waller said in a speech in London.
He added that if the October inflation data comes out higher than expected, then stronger action may be needed. "In that case, I believe a 50-basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered at the December meeting," Waller said. "Hiking only 25 basis points would put our credibility at risk, a risk I am not eager to take."
The latest CPI data is out, and the report showed that inflation came in hotter than expected in October but still cooled from the previous month.

articles.title_zh: Changes are coming to Social Security in January — here’s what Americans should know
articles.content_orig:
Starting in January, Social Security recipients will see two major changes.
The Social Security Administration (SSA) — a program providing financial benefits to eligible workers after reaching retirement age — will increase benefits and taxes. Back in October, the SSA announced that recipients will see a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) .
The COLA is the yearly increase meant to help Social Security keep up with rising prices.
This means nearly 72 million retirees will most likely see their Social Security benefits increase by about $75 per month starting in January. The increased payments will hit roughly 7.3 million people receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI) beginning on December 31, 2026.
Another change to hit millions of beneficiaries — some added taxes. Based on increases in average wages, the maximum amount of income subject to Social Security will increase next year.
For example, the maximum amount of earnings subject to the Social Security tax — known as taxable maximum — is set to increase from $184,500 to $192,300 in 2027.
The move will impact higher earners, as many will soon start paying Social Security taxes on an additional $7,800 in reported income. For example, someone earning at least $192,300 would likely pay up to $483.60 more annually in Social Security taxes.
The agency has recently announced another revision — the biggest change in its 91-year history . The SSA revealed it has officially “cleaned up” the comprehensive Social Security Number (SSN) database.
SSA records are referenced by federal government agencies and in states to validate identities — which helps prevent improper payments of taxpayer dollars. While it may seem like a small, administrative change, the move safeguards identity data, helps to prevent fraud and preserves proper program administration.
According to the office, it added 17 million dates of death to records that previously lacked this information, updated about 25 million records that previously had missing citizenship information and more.
For most recipients, it’s business as usual. No Social Security numbers have been taken; your monthly checks are still coming and recipients will still see a COLA bump.
To view your COLA notice online, head to your Social Security account. If you receive paperless notices, you may view and save your COLA notice in the “Message Center” starting in late November.
However, you must create an online “my Social Security account” and enroll in paperless notices by November 18 to see yours online. The agency will send paper notices with updated benefit amounts in early December.
And don’t forget — you may see an early Social Security check as Veterans Day falls on a Wednesday.

articles.title_orig: Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 is better than expected, but it needs some more optimization
articles.title_zh: Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 is better than expected, but it needs some more optimization
articles.content_orig:
Metaphor: ReFantazio , our RPG of the Year 2024 , launches this week on Nintendo Switch 2 following the recent release of the prologue demo . Ahead of its launch, I've been playing Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 for about a week and revisiting the PS5, PS4, and Steam versions across platforms to see how the final build of the Switch 2 port looks and feels. Note that the demo only featured one graphics mode from the final game: balanced. With that in mind, Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 is better than I expected, but it needs more work.
I say better because Persona 3 Reload launched in a pretty miserable state all things considered. Persona 3 Reload is also a less demanding game compared to Metaphor: ReFantazio which still has technical issues on consoles to this day. In fact, the only way to get a solid 60fps experience or smooth performance on consoles has been the PS4 version on PS5 or playing on PS5 Pro with VRR. This brings us to Nintendo Switch 2.
Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 arrives at a lower asking price than other versions, though they will all see price drops alongside the Switch 2 release. In terms of features, it has the same feature set as the console version with the addition of touchscreen support. The dash toggle present on PC that lets you dash by pressing a button instead of holding it is not present here. In that sense, Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 is closer to the console versions feature wise.
Metaphor: ReFantazio's demo had no graphics options. Atlus says it uses the "balanced" mode. Metaphor: ReFantazio's demo was a confusing release with how it looked good in some ways, but lacking in others. It also had inconsistent performance. The full game offers two additional visual options, but has some of the same issues as the demo. Metaphor: ReFantazio across all three visual modes runs with an uncapped frame rate targeting 60fps. This means you could be using the prioritize "graphics" mode and have a variable experience where it can hit 60fps indoors or while looking at the ground, but it is much lower in other areas. This also applies to the menus in-game which vary in responsiveness thanks to the frame rate.
If you played the demo, which is balanced mode, you likely noticed how it felt like upscaling was only being applied to one axis with the other looking like it uses interlacing or something you'd see back in the PS3 generation. Performance mode on Switch 2 appears to have the issue in both the horizontal axis and vertical axis.
Metaphor: ReFantazio's Switch 2 performance mode runs a lot better than the graphics mode, but it doesn't hit a solid frame rate. It also looks quite awful all things considered. Given the game's aesthetic and issues on other consoles, the best way to play it on Switch 2 is the graphics mode. It has the best and most stable visuals. If this mode gets patched with an optional 30fps cap and some optimization, it will be my preferred way to play Metaphor: ReFantazio on console in general because of the issues other consoles have.
For some background, Metaphor: ReFantazio on PS5 (and PS5 Pro since it never got Pro enhancements) ran with a 1656p resolution as per Digital Foundry . When I played it on my 1440p display, it looked good, but had a lot of shimmering since there was no anti-aliasing. The PS4 Pro version, which is also how it runs on PS5 via backward compatibility, dropped the resolution to 1080p and had a lot of cuts to shadows, draw distance, and more. The PS4 and PS5 versions have no graphics modes or anything to tweak. The PC version had one ace up its sleeve, and it is a brute force solution. You could downsample from a higher resolution if your hardware was capable enough to get cleaner visuals.
On Switch 2, we have an experience that sits in between PS4 and PS5, but it has one major advantage: temporal stability. The Switch 2 has less shimmering than all other console versions during movement. The downside is the overall resolution though. Even the UI on Switch 2 renders like the PS4 version's UI. Thankfully, the Switch 2 even in its performance mode (that looks awful) has better draw distance than the PS4 version.
When it comes to performance, the only way to get a stable 60fps on console is playing the PS4 version on PS5. If you play the PS5 version on PS5 Pro, it is a mostly solid 60fps, but not perfect. There are minor drops. This is still a massively better experience than playing the PS5 version on PS5, Xbox Series version on Xbox Series X or the Switch 2 version in any of its three modes. I'm surprised Atlus didn't add a frame rate cap option, but it seems like that ship has sailed for other platforms. Since the Switch 2 port is new, I hope it gets added in updates as a 30 or 40fps (at 120hz) would be amazing on Switch 2 and make it my preferred console version.
Right now it is a bit too unstable for my liking and with how long the load times are. Metaphor on Steam Deck can deliver better visuals since you can downsample, but you aren't getting a locked 60fps experience there with good visuals. Thankfully you can cap it to 30 or 40 and get a solid portable experience. It can go much higher, but the bigger cities and final dungeon run a lot worse if you want to play at 1080p downsampled or 720p with higher settings.
To test load times, I installed Metaphor: ReFantazio on the Switch 2 internal storage, the PS5 version on PS5 internal storage and PS4 Pro internal storage, the PS4 version on PS5 internal storage, and the Steam version on the Steam Deck OLED internal storage. I measured the time taken to get to the title screen from the dashboard, loading a save, and area transition time. I tested area transition time because it felt too long in the Switch 2 demo. The results below are in seconds and I mashed confirm to speed up the loading and skip any cut-scenes.
As you can see, the Switch 2 has the fastest initial load, but is the slowest when in-game. The PS5 version on PS5 Pro is the bestest in-game followed by the PS5 version. I hope the area transition and other load times when in-game on Switch 2 can be improved in updates.
Aside from no frame rate caps which I hope get added as options, Metaphor: ReFantazio's load times are a bit too long when in-game. Beyond this, I would like to see the UI support higher resolutions and at least have the menus run at 60fps if the gameplay itself is lower. The variable performance affecting menus and responsiveness is annoying.
In its current state, Metaphor: ReFantazio on Switch 2 is a lot better than I expected, but more work needs to be done. The visual options are good to have, but it looks quite rough in its performance mode. It also doesn't help that despite the downgrades to visuals in that mode, it can't hit a stable frame rate. I recommend playing with the quality mode enabled and tolerating the inconsistent performance for the best possible experience on Switch 2 right now. I do appreciate that the overall image is more temporally stable than other consoles at least. Hopefully Atlus continues to optimize and update this because performance caveats aside, Metaphor: ReFantazio is solid enough all things considered.

articles.title_orig: CoreWeave earnings put debt-fueled AI build-out under scrutiny
articles.title_zh: CoreWeave earnings put debt-fueled AI build-out under scrutiny
articles.content_orig:
CoreWeave faces a pivotal test when it reports its third-quarter financial results after the bell on Tuesday.
The market will be closely watching what the neocloud company says about artificial intelligence spending — and how it plans to finance its infrastructure buildout. The outcome could either calm concerns over its debt or stoke more fear.
"Investors need neoclouds to quantify how much financing they expect to raise to execute on existing backlog," Wolfe Research said in a note Monday. "We think outlooks that communicate when and which avenues of funding will be tapped will increase investor confidence."
CoreWeave stock and bonds have come under pressure as fears deepened about the enormous amount of debt it has taken out to build its data centers.
Its stock is down roughly 40% over the past month. Meanwhile, the yield on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 was 15.5% on Tuesday, after jumping to 16.7% on Thursday as investors digested the election results and possible roadblocks to data center construction. Bond yields move inversely to prices.
The spread on its five-year credit default swaps — which is insurance against default and considered a barometer of perceived credit risk — is also at levels that are considered distressed. On Tuesday, its CDS spread stood around 1,152 basis points, after rising above its October peak to close at 1,278 basis points on Thursday. Rising CDS spreads mean investors view the debt as riskier.
In addition, the New Jersey-based company's leverage is high. CoreWeave has a debt-to-equity ratio of 702%, up from almost 291% a year ago.
CEO Michael Intrator has sought to quell investor fear, posting on LinkedIn after the election last week that the company doesn't anticipate "any impact to CoreWeave's existing customer commitments or associated backlog as a result of shifts in the political landscape."
The company reported a revenue backlog of $104.2 billion in the second quarter . It has about $35 billion in debt, as of June 30.
CoreWeave has already given a picture of what it expects for the third quarter.
It guided for quarterly revenue of $3.4 billion to $3.6 billion when it reported second-quarter results in August. It anticipated capital expenditures between $11.5 billion and $13.5 billion for the quarter and $35 billion to $39 billion for the full year. The company also expects 1.85 gigawatts in active power by year-end.
Wells Fargo expects the company's capex needs for the rest of the year to be largely covered by its remaining undrawn debt, debt issuances in August/September and the $12 billion it is holding for project costs, which will flow into capex, analyst Michael Turrin said in a note Sunday.
However, its 2027 capex could reach $66 billion, based on an expected capacity addition of 1.5 gigawatts, Turrin said. That will require at least $25 billion more in debt, he noted. It can be largely funded through delayed draw term loans, which allows CoreWeave to draw down funds over time, and the rest can come through bonds and convertibles, he said.
Turrin has an overweight rating and $115 price target on the stock, implying 135% upside from Monday's close.
"While neoclouds sit in the eye of the AI storm, we remain confident that CRWV is the highest quality co in the space," Turrin wrote. "Beyond the noise, we see capacity/revs coming in better than expected (1.95GW this yr vs guide 1.85GW) as margins start to inflect."
However, investors likely won't get all the answers they're seeking during CoreWeave's third-quarter results, said CreditSights analyst Jordan Chalfin.
"One of the major issues for CoreWeave is whether or not they can obtain all the financing they need," he said. "They may try and calm the markets, but I'm not sure how much color they can and will provide."
Investors will be looking for 2027 guidance on capex and free cash flow, though that may not come until Coreweave releases fourth quarter results, Chalfin notes.
CoreWeave could ease investor concerns by showing it has plans and approvals in place to scale capacity through 2027, he said. The company can also demonstrate remaining performance obligation (RPO) growth, which shows the total value of its contracted future revenue, and highlight new customer wins.
In addition, pricing has been really strong on recent deals, Chalfin pointed out. "That could show up in an operating margin beat for Q3 and expectations for Q4."
While CoreWeave faces finances challenges, the company has many ways to access capital, Chalfin said. That includes chip-backed deals, which allow Corewave to borrow money using GPUs as collateral, and original equipment manufacturer financing. For instance, CoreWeave could turn to Dell , which is a big supplier with a strong balance sheet, Chalfin noted.
"Despite all the market sentiment, fundamentals are actually quite strong and pricing is strong," he said. "The trends over the next few quarters, I think, should be supportive." Risks could arise after that, but it is "too early to call."
Some analysts remain skeptical that Coreweave will be able to calm credit fears.
Bob Lang, founder and chief strategist at Explosive Options, points out that the company is facing a huge bill in just over two years. CoreWeave owes roughly $15 billion in principal payments through 2028, according to its second-quarter earnings statement .
"They don't have enough cash to service all that debt," he said. "Unless some big orders come in, unless some big money flows come in for them in the next 17, 18 months, I think this is going to be the start of the end for CoreWeave, unless somebody comes in and wants to buy them. But who wants to buy all that debt?"
However, there could be a "small" window for the company to push out its debt for another three to five years, but it will depend on how strong their cash flow is when they report on Tuesday, Lang said.
Plus, issuing equity to help fund infrastructure projects, like Meta and Oracle did recently , isn't an option for CoreWeave, he noted.
"They're going to dilute the stock so much that it's going to continue to go down," he said. "They missed that window when the stock was in the hundreds."
CoreWeave topped $183 in June 2025. It has since declined more than 73%, recently trading around $47.
Despite the fall, analysts remain bullish on the stock with an average overweight rating and $126 target, based on 39 estimates complied by FactSet.
—CNBC's Jordan Novet contributed reporting.

articles.title_orig: Toyota’s Scion Brand Returns With Japan’s Forbidden-Fruit Minitrucks
articles.title_zh: Toyota’s Scion Brand Returns With Japan’s Forbidden-Fruit Minitrucks
articles.content_orig:
Apparently, Toyota has been up at night watching Instagram reels. Reading the comments. Scratching its chin. Asking itself an important question: If people are already paying tariffs and other import fees to get old kei trucks into America from Japan, why don’t we just build new ones here?
That brings us to the Scion KEI-01. A small truck. With a tiny engine. And big dreams. What’s essentially a rebadged Daihatsu Hijet Jumbo, the Scion will instead be assembled at the same Toyota plant where the Grand Highlander and Sienna are built, in Princeton, Indiana. The word “kei” comes from the Japanese vehicle classification “keijidōsha,” which translates to light automobile.
See all results for used Toyota for sale near 94043
For now, you won’t find any hiding in the shadow of a lifted Toyota Tundra TRD Pro on dealer lots. Instead, these trucks—shorter than a Mazda MX-5 Miata —will be sold next year through a fleet-focused trial program to test the waters. If demand is strong, Toyota says limited retail sales could follow.
The Scion KEI-01 is as adorable as it looks and is said to weigh less than 2000 pounds, despite having all-wheel drive. Power comes from a tiny 660-cc three-cylinder engine paired with a continuously variable automatic transmission. It uses an independent front suspension, a solid rear axle, and a hydromechanical clutch to automatically shift power between the front and rear wheels based on traction needs. There’s also a “Lock” button to keep power evenly distributed between both axles.
The example Toyota showcased at a media event was equipped with tiny 145/80-12 Yokohama Super Van 355 tires. Its four-lug steel wheels, which almost hide the rear drum brakes, are roughly two inches smaller in diameter than the front brake rotors on the GR Corolla .
Here’s the catch. Just like another mini car—the Fiat Topolino —the Scion is restricted to low-speed duty, effectively making it a mullet-shaped golf cart. Top speed is limited to just 25 mph. Engineers tell us they baked this into the engine’s computer, and a simple “cut the wire” trick won’t unlock highway speeds. Its lack of speed is exactly how Toyota managed to get the KEI-01 into the U.S. so quickly. By meeting federal low-speed vehicle safety requirements, it can avoid the crash-test standards required of conventional passenger vehicles and pickups, retain its right-hand-drive layout, and stay as cute as a button.
See all results for used Toyota for sale near 94043
Measuring just over 11 feet long and less than five feet wide, the KEI-01 features a three-way folding cargo bed that can haul up to 600 pounds. That bed measures six feet six inches if you include the area under the cab, or five feet five inches without.
It comes with air conditioning, reclining seats, and push-button ignition. It will be sold with a cab-mounted reverse camera and may offer a towing package as optional equipment. Yes, it’s got airbags, though not many. Full pricing and options are still very TBD, as production is slated to begin in mid 2027.
The future of the Scion brand has also begun to take shape as a “freedom lab.” Toyota is using the name not as a conventional reboot, but as an outlet for experimental mobility ideas, such as a truck that measures just 11 feet in length.
Alongside the KEI-01, Toyota showed off its SxS Concept (previously revealed at SEMA last year), a side-by-side off-roader packing a turbocharged hybrid inline-four engine with more than 300 horsepower, and the BKE Concept scooter that already looks leagues more comfortable to ride than Honda’s Motocompacto .
It might not initially look like it, but the KEI-01 fits rather comfortably as a Scion. The original Scion brand spent its first life trying to convince young people to buy Toyotas. They wanted people to swap wheels, add racing stripes, and personalize an affordable car. That’s exactly what many people already do with their kei trucks. Just ask the guy baking wood-fired pizzas from the back of his Subaru Sambar if tiny trucks are any fun.
Austin Irwin has worked for Car and Driver for over 10 years in various roles. He's steadily worked his way from an entry-level data entry position into driving vehicles for photography and video, and is now reviewing and testing cars. What will he do next? Who knows, but he better be fast.

articles.title_orig: Samsung Gallery officially adds Google Photos backup, but not for all Galaxy users
articles.title_zh: Samsung Gallery officially adds Google Photos backup, but not for all Galaxy users
articles.content_orig:
Samsung has officially launched Google Photos integration in its Gallery app with backup services, and it’s also now widely rolled out for Galaxy devices.
Samsung Gallery started rolling out support for Google Photos backup in September, but it wasn’t widely available at the time. As of this week, though, Samsung is officially announcing the feature as it is now available broadly to Galaxy users.
“Gallery Sync” in the Samsung Gallery app replaces the previous Microsoft OneDrive integration with Google Photos, letting users sign in with their Google account of choice and use the free 15GB or paid Google One storage to back up photos and videos. This allows the Samsung Gallery app to show media backed up from another Galaxy device, but it doesn’t integrate your full Google Photos library.
At this point, Google Photos backup via Samsung Gallery should be broadly available to Galaxy owners. We’re seeing Samsung’s pop-up (pictured above) about the feature on our Galaxy Z Fold 8, with the feature fully functional beyond that.
You can also access setup via Menu > Settings > “Sync photos and videos” in the Samsung Gallery app.
Samsung requires your device to be running One UI 9 (Android 17) to access this feature, though it says that support will be “expanding to additional Galaxy devices in phases.” For the time being, though, that means the feature is a bit limited for users, as the One UI 9 rollout is still in progress.
Once media has been backed up to Google Photos, Samsung Gallery also now has a “free up space” button that can delete the local copies of your photos and videos to open up storage on your phone.

articles.title_orig: Take-Two talks about GTA 6 competing with Zelda: Ocarina of Time
articles.title_zh: Take-Two talks about GTA 6 competing with Zelda: Ocarina of Time
articles.content_orig:
Grand Theft Auto VI has been one of the most highly anticipated video game releases of the year since before it ever had an official release date. Grand Theft Auto V hit shelves in September 2013, more than 13 years ago, and since then, gamers have been wondering if they would ever get a sequel. After many delays and hiccups, Rockstar Games finally confirmed that GTA 6 will drop on November 19, 2026.
This isn't the only massive game coming out this month, though. Another heavy hitter, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , is also dropping on November 5. Ocarina of Time is a full-fledged remake of the 1998 Zelda classic of the same name. The original Ocarina of Time is considered to be one of the greatest games ever created, so Grand Theft Auto VI has some serious competition. CBR readers have weighed in on the GTA 6 vs. Ocarina of Time debate, sharing which they're looking forward to more.
Recently, CBR readers were asked to vote for which video game they would be spending the most time playing this month. The options were The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, Grand Theft Auto VI , and an option for other games and new releases. With how much hype GTA 6 has received over the last few years, many gamers might expect it to be a clear winner in this category, but the results don't actually reflect that.
According to the official results of the poll, 27.3% of CBR readers reported that they would be playing Grand Theft Auto VI . The same poll shows that an even 30% of readers would be playing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time instead. Needless to say, 30% isn't that much higher than 27.3%, but 2.7% more CBR readers are still more interested in the remake of this legendary Zelda game than the long-awaited GTA sequel.
The last 42.7% of CBR readers who voted on the poll reported that they would be spending their November playing something else. There are a few other big releases coming out this month. As the month right before the Christmas season, many gaming companies are releasing big titles that can be gifted for the upcoming holidays. A few other big contenders include World of Warcraft Forever (Nov 4), Guardians of the Galaxy Encore Edition (Nov 6), Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy (Nov 12), and Metaphor: ReFantazio (Nov 12), just to name a few.
It's not all that surprising that the "something else" category reigned supreme here, because many gamers won't want to be limited to just Ocarina of Time or GTA 6 . What some readers might find surprising, however, is the way GTA 6 came in dead last in the poll. There are probably a few factors working against GTA 6 here, with the most obvious being its release date. GTA 6 comes out on November 19 , which is weeks after Ocarina of Time . Many gamers who are planning to play both might have voted for Ocarina of Time because it comes out first.
There are some other things working against GTA 6 here, though. While Grand Theft Auto is an incredibly popular series, it's also a much more mature franchise dealing with themes like crime, extreme violence, sex, and potentially sensitive or triggering subjects. It caters to a more specific audience of gamers than Legend of Zelda fans, who range from young gamers, to fans who have been around since the '80s.
Perhaps the most obvious answer for why GTA 6 came in last, however, is how many issues the game has faced during production. Its official release date has been pushed back and delayed twice. Originally, the game was supposed to hit shelves in Fall 2025, an entire year ago. It was first pushed to May 2026, and then November. On top of the delays, it's also been the subject of multiple controversies, like its extremely expensive Collector's Edition that doesn't actually come with the game , and its uncertainty of an online multiplayer mode like the one that helped GTA 5 retain its popularity over the last 13 years.
There are a lot of reasons gamers might have been soured by Grand Theft Auto VI's lengthy and problematic production time, but at the end of the day, it's going up against a remake of one of the greatest video games ever made. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time isn't just one of the best Zelda games in the franchise, but one of the most highly praised video games ever made. Metacritic even has Ocarina of Time ranked as the #1 best game of all time.
It's not surprising that more CBR readers decided to vote for a game that is sure to be a smashing success. Early reviews of the remake are glowing and have already reinforced the idea that Ocarina of Time is a contemporary masterpiece that streamlines the 1998 game, while still keeping the heart and soul of the original intact.
Zelda is one of the most popular, identifiable, and influential video game franchises ever made, too. The original Legend of Zelda was released in 1986, and after 40 solid years, the series is more loved than ever. The Ocarina of Time remake isn't just a remake of one of the best games ever made, but also a celebration of 40 years of The Legend of Zelda , and it's no surprise that gamers of all ages are excited about playing it.
All that said, the truth is, Ocarina of Time and Grand Theft Auto VI are neck and neck. These two games are easily two of the biggest releases of 2026. Both games are going to sell millions of copies, spark discussions online among fans and gamers, and overall dominate the video game industry for the rest of the year and well into 2027. Even so, according to CBR readers, the Ocarina of Time remake is the more hotly-anticipated of the two games.

articles.title_orig: China’s trade surplus surpasses $1 trillion for a 2nd straight year, as exports surge 35%
articles.title_zh: China’s trade surplus surpasses $1 trillion for a 2nd straight year, as exports surge 35%
articles.content_orig:
China’s trade surplus surged past $1 trillion in the first 10 months as a global race to build AI infrastructure buoyed sales of high-tech products and helped offset weak domestic demand, a dynamic likely to sharpen tensions with major trading partners.
The figures highlight Beijing’s growing reliance on overseas demand to support an economy hobbled by subdued consumption and a protracted property slump. But while the global AI investment boom is expected to keep demand for Chinese technology products strong into 2027, it risks deepening domestic imbalances and fueling trade frictions with partners including the European Union.
Exports rose sharply by 35.2% in October from the same month last year in US dollar terms, customs data showed on Tuesday, only a touch slower than the 36.3% surge in September, but ahead of economists’ forecast for an increase of 33.5%.
That helped lift China’s trade surplus to $1.04 trillion in the first 10 months, topping $1 trillion for a second consecutive year and reaching the milestone a month earlier than in 2025.
Could China win the AI race?
The swelling surplus could fuel further tensions with the European Union , where leaders have called for more trade curbs with China after reaching an agreement with Beijing to limit Chinese exports of hybrid vehicles to the bloc over the next few years. Because the measures have yet to take effect, factories are expected to bring forward shipments, bolstering exports in the near term.
China economy grows thanks to AI export boom but domestic slump remains a drag
China on Monday officially announced the extension of a trade truce with Washington due to expire on November 10 by two months, but said last week that expanding its purchases of US farm goods would hinge on the implementation of their agreed reciprocal tariff-reduction arrangement.
“The risk of additional tariffs and other trade barriers will remain elevated in 2027, particularly as Chinese manufacturers continue expanding their presence in overseas markets,” said Joe Peissel, lead macroeconomist at Trivium China.
Imports grew 41.6%, beating the median forecast for a 32% increase in the Reuters poll and accelerating from the 31% growth in September.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit will take place next week in the southern Chinese tech and innovation hub Shenzhen, where Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump are expected to meet for the third time so far this year.
One big worry for Beijing is that consumers remain reluctant to spend, constrained by a property market downturn that has battered household wealth and dented confidence in the economic outlook.
Sluggish demand at home has pushed Chinese automakers to seek sales in overseas markets. China’s car exports maintained a solid pace of growth in October, while domestic vehicle sales recorded a 12th straight month of declines, separate data released by an industry association showed.
Greater reliance on exports, however, leaves China’s economy increasingly exposed to any slowdown in global demand.
Much of the strength in exports this year has been fueled by a global push to expand AI infrastructure.
“The outlook for exports depends on how long the AI boom will last,” Macquarie analysts wrote. They expect China’s exports to accelerate further in the fourth quarter before starting to slow from the first quarter of 2027.

articles.title_orig: EU budget battle erupts as four countries defy Merz over Ukraine aid
articles.title_zh: EU budget battle erupts as four countries defy Merz over Ukraine aid
articles.content_orig:
German chancellor has signalled he will block budget with no aid deal, complaining that burden is ‘carried mostly by only a few member states’
Friedrich Merz has signalled he will block the EU’s seven-year budget unless there is a deal on financial aid for Ukraine, triggering accusations of “typical blackmail” from some other European leaders and setting the stage for stormy talks later this month.
The German chancellor’s intervention has angered leaders in central Europe who are net beneficiaries of EU funds but do not want to take part in an upcoming funding round to support Ukraine’s war effort.
“What the chancellor is doing is typical blackmail, and I will not give in to it,” Slovakia’s Russia-friendly prime minister , Robert Fico, told reporters in Bratislava.
He was speaking alongside his Czech counterpart, Andrej Babiš, whose populist government also rejects taking part in a future loan for Ukraine. “I do not know why he is saying it,” Babiš said, referring to Merz’s position.
Merz wants EU leaders to discuss Ukraine’s financing needs at a summit in Dublin on Friday. “We must continue to support Ukraine in its fight to defend itself. This is in our shared vital interest,” he wrote in a letter, seen by the Guardian, to the European Council president, António Costa, who will chair the meeting. “And yet, bilateral assistance to Ukraine is distributed unevenly and carried mostly by only a few member states.”
The EU last year agreed to lend Ukraine €90bn , which was intended to cover two-thirds of its military and civilian costs for 2026 and 2027. But since then, Russia’s relentless bombardment has heaped more costs on Kyiv, prompting President Volodymyr Zelenskyy to call for €70bn to fill a budget shortfall .
The EU has endorsed Zelenskyy’s figures and pledged to find €45bn, with Ukraine’s other allies, such as the UK and Canada, expected to provide the rest.
Merz last year led an effort to use Russia’s €210bn sovereign wealth frozen in the EU, but the plan was scuppered by opposition led by Belgium, which hosts most of the funds at Brussels.
The €90bn loan was the fallback plan. Hungary, Slovakia and Czechia, which opted out of that loan, have indicated they will stay out of the next round. Those three member states have now been joined by Bulgaria, following the election of Moscow-friendly prime minister Rumen Radev last April.
The issue of Ukraine’s financing is now ricocheting into tortuous negotiations on the EU budget for 2028-34. Germany , the largest net contributor, wants steep cuts in the proposed budget, while opposing generous EU funding for member states that refuse to chip in to Ukraine’s financial needs.
In his letter Merz writes that “a collective commitment … without exception” is an “essential pre-requisite” for resolving Ukraine’s funding shortfall and “discussing any further matters, particularly those with financial implications”.
He also states that all member states need to contribute to a “sound” financial perspective for Ukraine from 2028 in the context of the EU’s next seven-year budget, known as the multiannual financial framework.
after newsletter promotion
A German government official said: “Financial support for Ukraine of all EU member states is essential in order to successfully complete the MFF.”
Berlin is also seeking to switch the decision-making process on funding Ukraine to a qualified-majority vote, rather than unanimity, in order to prevent one government from blocking EU decisions.
The letter reflects growing exasperation from the EU’s northern member states that are Ukraine’s most generous backers over smaller contributions from other EU member states in central and southern Europe.
The task of finding an agreement on the budget falls to Costa, a former Portuguese prime minister. He wants a deal by the end of the year, before elections in France, Poland and Italy in 2027 that are likely to complicate the task.
A spokesperson for Costa confirmed receipt of the letter without commenting on details. “President Costa will make time for interventions on Ukraine at the informal European Council in Dublin this week,” the spokesperson said, adding that Ukraine finance would be discussed at a special summit dedicated to the EU budget on 26-27 November.

Fresh details about the Ford Mustang Shelby GT350 successor suggest that the upcoming model will be offered exclusively as a coupe.
Unlike the more powerful Dark Horse SC, which is available with both a fixed roof and a soft-top convertible, the new variant will not get an open-top version. This also follows the approach taken with the previous S550-generation Shelby GT350, which was sold only as a coupe.
Pricing is expected to position the car between the standard Dark Horse and the Dark Horse SC. The 2026 Dark Horse starts at around $65,000, while the SC carries a much higher starting price of approx $106,000. A price in the $80,000 range could make sense for the new model, although Ford has yet to confirm anything.
Its official name remains under wraps, but the Dark Horse badge is expected to feature somewhere in it. The new Mustang is reportedly scheduled to reach dealerships in 2027 as a 2027 model-year offering.

articles.title_orig: Number of arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
articles.title_zh: Number of arrests made in Mohamed Al Fayed probe in France, police say
articles.content_orig:
French police have made arrests after three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris, were searched in relation to an investigation into Mohamed Al Fayed's abuse.
The Paris prosecutor's office told the BBC that several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released.
In a confidential letter sent to survivors, the Metropolitan Police said its officers were present during the searches on 13 and 14 October, in what is understood to be a joint operation between British and French authorities.
It is the first time any arrests have been made in relation to alleged abuse and trafficking by the former Harrods and Ritz owner.
Several victims of Al Fayed were also interviewed by French investigators, the prosecutor's office said.
It added that the searches were part of a preliminary investigation into "allegations of human trafficking committed by an organized group, aggravated pimping committed by an organized group, and rape".
The investigation is ongoing and digital material seized during the searches is being analysed.
The late Egyptian billionaire bought the Ritz Paris hotel in 1979, and it is still owned by the Al Fayed family.
The Villa Windsor in western Paris, another property involved in the search, was a holiday home for the Al Fayed family. It was previously the home of King Edward VIII, following his abdication, and his wife Wallis Simpson.
The Met shared this statement from French authorities with victims:
"At this stage of the proceedings, several victims have been interviewed by French investigators, and the investigations are being conducted in liaison with the British authorities.
"In this context, searches and evidence-gathering operations were carried out in mid-October 2026, notably within the Hotel Ritz in the 1st arrondissement of Paris, as well as at the Villa Sainte-Thérèse in Saint-Tropez, a former property of Mohamed Al Fayed, and at the Villa Windsor in the 16th arrondissement of Paris, in the presence of British investigators.
"Several suspects were taken into police custody, measures which were lifted following their interviews, specifically for the purpose of analyzing digital material seized during the search operations.
"The investigations are continuing under the direction of the Paris Public Prosecutor's Office."
A Met Police spokesperson confirmed its officers travelled to France in October and were present during the operation.
Al Fayed, who died in 2023 aged 94, was accused by more than 20 women of sexual assault in a BBC documentary and podcast in September 2024.
One of the women featured in the documentary said she was sexually assaulted by Al Fayed at the Ritz hotel in Paris, while another woman said she had been raped by him at the Villa Windsor residence.
Since those allegations, more than 400 alleged victims or witnesses have come forward to lawyers.
A woman has also told BBC Scotland she was trafficked, drugged, sexually assaulted and held prisoner on the Balnagown Estate by Al Fayed's brother , Salah Fayed, who died in 2010.
Both brothers died without facing legal charges in relation to these allegations.
Earlier this year, Police Scotland said it was carrying out further investigations into allegations connected to Balnagown Estate.
In a statement, a force spokesperson said: "Three people have been identified in connection with offending against a number of victims.
"Our inquiries are ongoing and it would be inappropriate to comment further."
The Justice for Fayed and Harrods Survivors group said it welcomed the "significant developments" and cooperation between the Met and French authorities.
"We believe that all properties owned by Fayed should be investigated with the same thoroughness as those already searched, wherever they are located, to ensure that no potentially relevant evidence is overlooked," the group said.
"We hope these developments represent meaningful progress towards identifying and holding to account all those who facilitated, concealed or assisted his offending, wherever they operated."
The survivor advocacy group No One Above said: "France is treating this as organised human trafficking, led by specialists, with properties searched and evidence seized. That is what a serious investigation into a network looks like.
"Two years on, survivors are still waiting for the same from the Met. It is time the National Crime Agency took this investigation over."
The management of the Ritz Paris told AFP news agency that it "does not tolerate any form of harassment, abuse or inappropriate behaviour" and that it was ready "to cooperate fully with the competent judicial authorities".
If you have been affected by any of the issues raised in this story, information and support is available at BBC Action Line .

articles.title_orig: Polestar has a new look with its Formula 2030 concept
articles.title_zh: Polestar has a new look with its Formula 2030 concept
articles.content_orig:
Perhaps only a small percentage of Ars readers will care about the Polestar 2030 concept, debuted today by the electric automaker. Spun out of Volvo—once upon a time, Polestar was a racing team—the brand has leveraged the resources of parent-automaker Geely to create electric vehicles that marry a modern minimalist style with rewarding driving dynamics . But you now can’t buy any Polestars in the US , since Geely is Chinese, and banning Chinese-owned car brands enjoys remarkable bipartisan support in Congress.
The Formula 2030 is about the same length as a Polestar 2 but with a very low roofline. If anything, the two-box shape reminds me of the Saab Aero-X, one of the final concepts from the then-terminal Swedish automaker. (In many ways, Polestar has adopted Saab’s mantle.)
Polestar says the concept fits into its own segment somewhere between the next Polestar 2 and the Polestar 7—it numbers its cars chronologically (mostly), not based on size—although it’s not saying if the hatchback design will go into series production. Successfully packaging rear-seat passengers and a lithium-ion battery pack is something a concept needn’t worry about, after all. Rather, it’s a styling exercise, or more than one.
The nose is a good preview of the next Polestar 2, and the rear light signature will show up on production Polestars. “We wanted to evolve, while respecting the core design values we demonstrated with previous models that define the Polestar brand in such a recognizable way,” said Nahum Escobedo, head of exterior design at Polestar.
“And with Formula 2030, with its clear Polestar design attributes, like the Dual Blade headlights, wraparound visor-like windshield, and powerful haunches, we have done just that. But we’ve pushed perceptions, preconceptions, and the expected as well, with our considered choices in form language, amplification of the performance topic, and new detailing, like the Single Blade rear lights,” Escobedo said.
Polestar says the four-seat interior pushes its usual minimalism even further. But the end result has avoided the bland fate suffered by the recent Range Rover GT concept, for example. Even though Polestar is committed to developing autonomous driving technology, for manual modes it has added physical controls—rocker switches and rotary controllers, with a user-configurable UI. That’s a new thing for Polestar.
You can’t really tell from the photos, but the Formula 2030 concept explores some sustainability ideas as well. Like BMW’s I Vision Circular , the Formula 2030 was designed using monomaterials and with recycling in mind where possible. The interiors of the doors are fully recyclable, there’s low-emission steel in the chassis, and biocomposites are used in place of traditional plastics.

articles.title_orig: 'Like gods reigning over humans': Many defectors see daughter of North Korea's Kim as heir apparent
articles.title_zh: 'Like gods reigning over humans': Many defectors see daughter of North Korea's Kim as heir apparent
articles.content_orig:
FILE - In this photo provided by the North Korean government, its leader Kim Jong Un, center, and his daughter, reportedly named Kim Ju Ae, visit a military training base in North Korea, Thursday, March 19, 2026. Independent journalists were not given access to cover the event depicted in this image distributed by the North Korean government. The content of this image is as provided and cannot be independently verified. 朝鮮通信社/KCNA via KNS via AP hide caption
SEOUL, South Korea — Until she fled North Korea three years ago, Kim Yumi felt deeply frustrated whenever state TV showed leader Kim Jong Un with his young daughter. The message, she felt, was clear and worrying: North Korea was laying the groundwork for an eventual hereditary transfer of power, this time to Kim's daughter.
Publicly questioning the Kim dynasty's hold on power would mean severe persecution. Already angered by draconian pandemic regulations that ruined her family's fishing business, she defected to South Korea by boat with her family.
"My husband and I didn't want our children to live under a fourth-generation dictatorship. As parents, we thought the best thing we could do for our children was to give them freedom," said Kim Yumi, 32, who now lives in Seoul.
North Korea allows no dissent and harshly punishes attempts to flee the country. Established in 1948, the nation is nominally a socialist republic, but in reality it is an authoritarian dynasty, with three generations of the Kim family ruling in succession. There was no known public resistance during its previous two successions — from state founder Kim Il Sung to his son Kim Jong Il in 1994 and then from Kim Jong Il to his son Kim Jong Un in 2011.
This time, North Korea is apparently trying something radical.
Kim Jong Un's repeated public appearances with his daughter over the past four years have led to speculation that she's being groomed as her father's heir.
The question of who will become North Korea's next leader is crucial because that person will face a huge challenge — governing an impoverished, nuclear-armed nation whose 26 million people have little political freedom and live under strict state surveillance while being cut off from much of the outside world.
North Koreans have no say in the selection of their future leader, and analysts and defectors say they will passively accept a third dynastic succession — at least publicly.
To gauge North Koreans' private views, The Associated Press spoke with nearly a dozen defectors who still have contacts in North Korea or witnessed the country's previous power successions, as well as several experts.
Not much is known about Kim's daughter except that she's reportedly about 13 and named Kim Ju Ae.
Since late 2022, she has made dozens of public appearances, all of them with her father at big events like weapons tests and military parades. State media has called her Kim's "most beloved" and "respected" child. Her status has been emphasized by images showing an elderly general kneeling before her and her standing in front of her father.
South Korea's spy agency says she is Kim's likely heir. Eight of the 11 defectors interviewed by the AP shared that view; the others disagreed, citing the North's deeply patriarchal culture.
"During her visits to missile launch sites and factories, the way senior North Korean officials treat Kim Ju Ae involves protocols reserved for a successor, not the ones simply for a daughter of Kim Jong Un," said Tae Yongho, a former minister at North Korea's Embassy in London who defected to South Korea in 2016. "They are repeating the same protocol and treatment they provided for Kim Jong Un," when he accompanied his father as his heir.
Tae Yongho, a former minister of North Korea's Embassy in London who defected to South Korea in 2016, speaks during an interview with The Associated Press in Seoul, South Korea, Thursday, Oct. 22, 2026. Lee Jin-man/AP hide caption
Kang Mi-Jin, a defector who runs a company analyzing North Korea's economy, said her contacts inside the North told her over smuggled phones that they think Kim Ju Ae is in line to succeed her father.
Jung Gwang-il, a defector who specializes in smuggling outside information to North Korea, said the North Koreans he meets as they visit Chinese border towns also hold the same belief.
Former NBA star Dennis Rodman was the first to reveal her identity, holding her as a baby during a 2013 trip to Pyongyang.
Much of the skepticism about Kim Ju Ae as a potential leader stems from her being female. South Korean officials believe she has a younger sibling whose gender hasn't been confirmed.
Women in North Korea remain deeply underrepresented in senior posts. Only one of 17 department directors for the ruling Workers' Party is a woman. That woman is Kim Jong Un's influential younger sister, Kim Yo Jong, according to South Korea's Unification Ministry.
"My contacts in North Korea say it would be nonsensical to revere that little girl as their supreme leader," said Kim Jeong-Ah, a former North Korean army officer who resettled in South Korea in 2009.
Lee Si-young, a defector who heads the Seoul-based Free North Korea Radio station, said that some of her older contacts in North Korea aren't happy with a woman taking power. But she said members of the Kim family "are like gods reigning over humans so gender really doesn't matter."
Whether or not the girl succeeds her father, observers agree that Kim Jong Un, 42, is likely to designate one of his children to prolong his family's rule, a move they expect would face little resistance at home. South Korea's spy agency recently assessed that Kim is extremely obese and at high risk of cardiovascular disease but shows no other signs of poor health.
North Koreans will passively "accept a hereditary succession as something that they should go along with," said Ahn Chan-il, a defector and scholar who heads the World Institute for North Korean Studies in Seoul.
During North Korea's first leadership transition, in 1994, the new leader, Kim Jong Il, then 52, had already spent two decades as the official successor working alongside his father to run the country.
The second succession, in 2011, was more uncertain. Kim Jong Un, who was then 27, was seen by outsiders as too young and inexperienced. He quickly consolidated his grip on power, however, by orchestrating high-profile executions and purges, including the 2013 killing of his powerful uncle Jang Song Thaek.
"A hereditary power succession system has been institutionalized in North Korea, just like presidential elections in our system," said Oh Gyeong-seob, an analyst at Seoul's Korea Institute for National Unification. "North Korea's ruling elite accepts it as a matter of course. So do its general citizens."
Choi Song-juk, who fled North Korea in 2015, said she had been so brainwashed that she had no complaints about the North's two earlier power successions. She now calls them "nonsense."
Defector Jeon Jae-hyun said North Korea's pervasive surveillance apparatus keeps people from voicing their discontent with the government and helps enforce political loyalty.
Defector Kim Yumi said she had never heard about the girl until Kim Jong Un publicly introduced his daughter at a long-range missile launch site in November 2022.
"Ordinary people know absolutely nothing about private lives of the Kim family," said Kim Yumi, who now runs a YouTube channel on North Korea. "They don't really try to know about it and don't pay attention to it because doing so could put them in danger."
